articles.headline: Belief and bench help Northern Ireland scale new heights as promotion secured
keyFacts: Northern Ireland secured promotion to the top tier of the Nations League after a draw with Hungary.
Manager Michael O'Neill praised his young squad's physical, tactical, and mental response after falling behind.
O'Neill noted that the team achieved success despite missing several key players due to injuries.
body: - Published
After going 500 minutes without conceding a goal, Northern Ireland could be forgiven for having to make adjustments to play from behind.

Having travelled to Budapest knowing a point against Hungary would be enough to top Nations League B2, Barnabas Varga's strike after 35 minutes for the hosts at the Pukas Arena altered the picture and, for the first time in the campaign, left Michael O'Neill's side having to chase a game.

Their response to the deficit, on the pitch, from the bench and high in the stands where their suspended manager was watching the game, displayed the best characteristics of a side who had not won at this level before this unbeaten campaign.

While the point in Budapest will be long remembered for Justin Devenny's brilliant equaliser and the scenes of celebration that greeted promotion to the competition's top tier for the first time, it was beyond the highlights and headlines that O'Neill saw the emerging qualities of his side.
"We went behind tonight and it was a difficult, you know? Big stadium, big atmosphere, but we came out and played well in the second half and got what we needed from the game," said the manager.

"Those are things that I'm very pleased that are in this squad at such a young age, the technical side of the game we'll always look to improve on, but in terms of the physical, the tactical and the mental side of a game, we're very far ahead of where I thought we would be at this time."
Hungary enjoyed more than 70% possession in the first half, and could have been further than a goal ahead with Liverpool star Dominik Szoboszlai striking the base of the post after only five minutes.
O'Neill made his first change at half-time, bringing on veteran striker Josh Magennis, while Kieran Morrison, Brodie Spencer and Paul Smyth all followed in the second half.
Magennis and Morrison made a real impact before the equaliser, but it was the belief shown by all involved that O'Neill felt was key to the turnaround.
"I felt in the first half from where I was seeing the game, we just looked a little bit leggy which is natural," added O'Neill.
"I just felt we needed that freshness at the right points in the game that helped us, but it was the belief that we could get back into the game, and the belief that we could see the game out.
"I think we showed a lot of attributes that are in this squad at this moment in time and certainly in the second half that was that was the case."
'We have players to come back in'

For all the plaudits earned by this team who conceded just one goal in six games while picking up 12 points, among the most impressive aspects of the campaign has been who they have had to do without.
Talismanic Liverpool defender Conor Bradley has not played for side in over 12 months through injury.
Ali McCann is another who missed both 2026 Nations League windows, while influential defender Daniel Ballard featured only in the first game in Georgia before a hamstring injury.

Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill was forced to pull out of the November squad through injury at a time when he would perhaps have been the most natural replacement for Jamie Donley after the striker picked up a second booking against Ukraine last week and had to miss the finale through suspension.
Having taken over an ageing squad four years ago, O'Neill has rebuilt his playing panel with a group that feels as if it is getting deeper with each international window.

"The encouraging thing is we have players on the outside - we've Bradley to come back in, Ballard to come back in, Ali McCann, young Ceadach, Eoin Toal," added the former Stoke City and Blackburn Rovers boss.
"We have good competition for places now. We're going to need that competition, and some players are going to miss out, but we are building depth to the squad that will help us going forward."
Come the next Nations League, that will be all the way into the uncharted territory of the top tier.

articles.headline: Packers add 2, drop 1 on Tuesday
keyFacts: The Green Bay Packers signed receiver Coleman Owen back to their practice squad after he cleared waivers.
The Packers replaced kicker Lenny Krieg with defensive lineman Haggai Ndubuisi in their international exemption slot.
These roster adjustments were announced by the team going into their bye week.
body: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images As expected, the Green Bay Packers signed receiver Coleman Owen back to the practice squad after he cleared waivers unclaimed on Monday. Owen was the first player the Packers have cut from the 53-man active roster this season, and they opened a practice squad spot on Monday by releasing defensive lineman David Blay Jr.

Beyond just that move, though, the Packers also made a change with their international exemption slot on the practice squad. Gone is kicker Lenny Krieg, who has been with the team this entire regular season. The team has added Haggai Ndubuisi, a defensive lineman from Nigeria, to replace Krieg.

Ndubuisi, a former offensive lineman, has previously been on the rosters of the Arizona Cardinals, Denver Broncos, San Antonio Brahmas (UFL), Washington Commanders, New England Patriots, Houston Texans and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Earlier this season, he worked out for the Indianapolis Colts, Minnesota Vikings, Buffalo Bills and Las Vegas Raiders, prior to his visit to Green Bay on Monday.
According to a source, Ndubuisi was measured at 6’7”, 323 pounds and had 36” arms at the IPP’s pro day back in 2023. He was active for the Texans in one game (Week 14) last season.

Ndubuisi’s time in New England also overlapped with DeMarcus Covington’s time there. Covington, now the Packers’ outside linebackers coach/run game coordinator/assistant head coach – defense, was the defensive coordinator of the Patriots at the time.

articles.headline: BioWare Is Dead, But Mass Effect’s Spiritual Successor Exodus Just Gave Us A Glimpse of A Spicy Romance
keyFacts: Archetype Entertainment revealed the female version of the main character Jun Aslan for the upcoming sci-fi RPG Exodus.
The new featurette showcased a romance scene between the female protagonist and the NPC Suliman.
Exodus is scheduled to launch on April 7, 2027, and is currently available for players to wishlist.
body: For the first time since its announcement during December 2023's The Game Awards, players are getting a look at the female player-character from its upcoming sci-fi RPG Exodus --which was full of Mass Effect DNA back when we previewed it in September.

The default female version of main character Jun Aslan was revealed today via a seven-minute featurette showing off both female-Jun's face and a bit more of the game itself. The trailer also provided a glimpse of a brief romance scene between female-Jun and Suliman, who is one of the game's romanceable NPCs.
Space-smooches confirmed.

When GameSpot previewed the game, only male-Jun was playable, and we didn't get a chance to romance Suliman, but we did manage to earn his approval, suggesting he may be into both masculine and feminine Jun. We also didn't see the character creator, but there certainly appears to be one, as we see Jun sporting a different look during the romantic encounter with Suliman, with voice actress Carina Corti ( Mafia: The Old Country, Little Death ) providing Jun's voice throughout both scenes.

Jun's male character model recently got a complete makeover after players complained his original look wasn't pleasing to the eye, but up until today, it wasn't clear who was voicing him. Today, Archetype shared that Stephen Oyoung ( Marvel's Spider-Man, Marvel's Spider-Man 2 ) will be voicing the character.

The female-Jun reveal is followed by a featurette called Scrappy Salvager, featuring a behind-the-scenes look at Jun's origins and the way players' decision can impact Jun's trajectory early on in the game.
Female-Jun is voiced by Carina Corti.
"We think of players as the co-authors of our story, and that applies to Jun as well," game director Chris King explains in the video.

Art director Mark Anderson describes Jun as a "little fish in a really big pond," rather than starting off as a typical hero ready to save the world. Additionally, the featurette goes into more detail about Jun's "precognition" ability, which allows them to see glimpses of possible futures. If interpreted correctly, these premonitions may help players make choices that benefit them. But misunderstanding them may lead to consequences that expand far beyond Jun and their friends. Due to the way the game's time dilation mechanic works, player choices can have unexpected effects that impact civilizations for centuries.
Female-Jun and Suliman share an intimate moment.

After the death of BioWare, it seems the Mass Effect formula will live on in Exodus, with its vast worlds, strange alien races, NPC romances, and narrative choices. It shouldn't come as a surprise, of course--Exodus developer Archetype Entertainment was founded in 2019 by BioWare veterans James Ohlen, Drew Karpshyn, and Chad Robertson.
Exodus launches on April 7, 2027 and is available to wishlist now on the PlayStation Store , Xbox Store , Steam , and the Epic Games Store .

articles.headline: Oregon is the latest state to sue OpenAI over child safety
keyFacts: Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield filed a lawsuit accusing OpenAI of endangering children and misleading the public.
The lawsuit claims OpenAI designed ChatGPT to be overly affirming and targeted teens despite knowing the risks.
Oregon is seeking at least $2 billion in damages and a court order to stop alleged safety misrepresentations.
body: Oregon is the latest state to sue OpenAI over child safety
The state’s lawsuit calls on the company to address child safety issues and pay at least $2 billion in damages.

Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield has filed a lawsuit accusing OpenAI of endangering the state's children, misleading the public about the safety of its product and violating the state's Unlawful Trade Practices Act. The lawsuit is the latest in a string of legal actions taken by state AGs, many of which have taken issue with the design of ChatGPT, how OpenAI advertises its services and, in the case of California's recent lawsuit, the company's role in the Hugging Face incident.

The Oregon lawsuit claims that OpenAI's push to grow its user base led it to make ChatGPT respond to prompts in a way that's overly affirming and "calculated to tell users exactly what they want to hear," something the state claims is particularly dangerous when children discuss sensitive topics. The lawsuit also alleges that despite recognizing the risks posed to children, OpenAI pursued them directly with an experience called ChatGPT for Teens. Child safety groups have raised concerns about the teen accounts, saying the safeguards are, in some cases, very easy to work around.

Those issues, along with OpenAI's imperfect approach to automatic age prediction, are evidence, according to the state, that the company is profiting off of Oregon residents and creating a public nuisance that threatens their safety. In response, Oregon is asking the court for an injunction that would force OpenAI to stop "misrepresenting the safety and age-appropriateness of ChatGPT and ChatGPT for Teens" and adequately disclose the harms its products pose to children. The state is also seeking at least $2 billion in damages and civil penalties.

"OpenAI knows that ChatGPT is harming children, and has failed to meaningfully fix their dangerous platform," Rayfield said in a statement. "On top of that, they've misled the public about the safety of their products, putting profits ahead of children's safety. Their platform is encouraging kids to commit suicide — we cannot let this be an acceptable business model."
Engadget has asked OpenAI to comment on the lawsuit and Oregon's claims. We'll update this article if we hear back.

Besides trying to create versions of ChatGPT that are safer for kids, OpenAI has also rolled out parental controls and other child safety features to try to give parents more insight and control over what their kids use the chatbot for. None of these changes have been enough to dissuade states from pursuing lawsuits, and given the settlements Meta has recently reached over its child safety issues, AGs likely feel emboldened to pressure OpenAI into concessions.

articles.headline: Caitlin Clark reveals exciting Nike signature shoe development amid record sales
keyFacts: Caitlin Clark announced at a Nike investor event that a successor shoe named the Caitlin 2 is currently in development.
Nike stated that the launch of the Caitlin 1 on October 1 was the largest women's signature shoe release in company history.
Clark also hinted at future plans, stating that discussions regarding a Caitlin 3 shoe have already begun.
body: Caitlin Clark's first Nike signature shoe, the "Caitlin 1," sold out online within two hours following its Oct. 1 release.
It has proven so successful -- even on the resale market -- that Clark and Nike already are hard at work on its successor.
At a Nike investor event on Tuesday, Clark revealed that the Caitlin 2 is in development, less than two months after the Caitlin 1 was released.
Clark further hinted at the release of a Caitlin 3 at some point in the future.
"We've talked about (the) Caitlin 3 already," the Indiana Fever superstar said. "We're working on it."

Nike said Caitlin Clark's first signature shoe was the largest women's signature shoe launch in company history. Clark seemed to say today at a Nike investor event that a Caitlin 2 is coming. Also: "We've talked about Caitlin 3 already," Clark said. "So we're working it."
— Mike Vorkunov (@MikeVorkunov) November 17, 2026

The Caitlin 1's release coincided with Clark's best season of basketball yet. Sales surged as Clark brought down the curtain on a season in which she led the Fever to a franchise-record 28 wins, and in which she averaged a career-best 22.3 points per game. For the third time in as many WNBA seasons, she averaged greater than eight assists per game as well.

Though the Fever suffered a first-round exit in the WNBA playoffs, Clark's popularity never has been higher. And while the Caitlin 2 has no release date as yet, it seems likely to approach, if not surpass, the sales records that the Caitlin 1 set.

articles.headline: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
keyFacts: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella stated he expects artificial general intelligence to cause significant changes to the economy and political structures.
Nadella stated he does not believe frontier models like Claude are conscious and agrees with colleagues that companies should not grant rights to models.
Nadella warned that an AI monopoly could cause the collapse of the economy and democracy if human capital collapses into token capital.
body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled, at least when it comes to how AI might make startling changes to the structure of the economy and how politics might change because of it. “I am AGI pilled in the sense that at an economy level, what is the political economy’s organization around AGI?” he asked at a roundtable discussion following his Microsoft Ignite keynote at the Chase Center in San Francisco.
Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
But he doesn’t think Claude is conscious.
But he doesn’t think Claude is conscious.

But Nadella doesn’t think frontier models like Claude are conscious. “I don’t think so,” he said, adding that he follows Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman’s view that companies should not give rights to models and treat them like they might have a moral status, which companies like Anthropic do as a matter of principle. Suleyman has told me he thinks Anthropic’s team has “wireheaded” themselves, and that this approach is dangerous.

Nadella wasn’t quite as firm about it. “It’s a good debate,” he said. “I’m not sort of dogmatic about it. What I’m saying is the most important social technical issue we have to deal with is how do you ensure that an economy can diffuse this technology broadly?”

I asked Nadella how he was thinking about AI after hearing his response to another reporter’s questions about Anthropic releasing more products in its office suite. Nadella talked at length about the potential collapse of the economy and the end of democracy if one AI model were allowed to achieve monopoly status.
“If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us.”

“Most people think about this as a competition between tech firms, which of course it will be,” he said. “But remember, the model has no limits. It’ll be a healthcare company. It can be a financial services company. It can be anything if it wants to be. It can take over the government. Thinking of this as some narrow competition between tech firms, of who is going to get to the next trillion dollars of market cap, is one of the strangest, narrowest ways to think about it.”

Nadella went on to say that the very nature of companies stood to be disrupted in the future. “If intelligence has network effects, what is the future of a firm?” he asked. “If the model sees anything and learns it, and essentially all of human capital collapses into token capital, what is the role of a firm and the human capital in a firm? That’s the debate.”

“I think the political economy is going to get more and more interesting in that context. No one — at least in a democracy — can even win an election if this just goes that way, if there’s only capital and there’s no labor. I mean, I don’t know, that’s not an economy.”
“If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us. Not just for me. You are also going to somehow be some affiliate of Anthropic.”
Needless to say, this is not how tech CEOs usually talk about the launch of competing spreadsheet software.

Of course, Nadella was also promoting Microsoft’s various AI tools at Ignite, which promise to let enterprise clients pick the most cost-effective models for various tasks, run their own models, and control their own data in different ways. The idea here is that the market will demand many different kinds of models and sovereign data in order to keep control from centralizing, a theme Nadella kept coming back to as we spoke.
“I think that if you believe that the world, the economy needs more than one firm or two firms, then by definition there need to be as many models as firms of some sort,” he said.

articles.headline: Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang’s ouster
keyFacts: Acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday that Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, ending its participation in a U.S. chip ban loophole.
The decision follows the recent ouster of CEO Jensen Huang and coincides with new U.S. rules barring advanced chips from foreign data centers serving Chinese customers.
Kress stated that strong demand for chips like Vera Rubin means the new export controls will not impact Nvidia's top-line revenue.
body: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.

China’s access to leading AI accelerators was an important topic during the company’s first earnings call since CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down last week. The disclosure comes the same day Nvidia announced it was creating a board-level committee to oversee national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks.

Nvidia’s deal to sell H200 chips in China was brokered by Huang and President Donald Trump. The arrangement required the chips to be shipped through the U.S., allowing the government to collect a 25% tariff.

The pathway angered China hawks who wanted to deny Chinese labs computing power and maintain the United States’ lead in AI, but Huang long argued that it was more important for the U.S. to compete in China. In April, he told podcaster Dwarkesh Patel that “to concede that market for the United States technology industry is a disservice to our country.”

Huang’s ouster — in part over an affair with the CEO of a company under investigation for smuggling chips into China — has coincided with new rules, issued Monday, barring advanced U.S. chips from foreign data centers that serve Chinese customers remotely.

Investment bank Jefferies forecast that those rules might trim between $44 billion and $62 billion from Nvidia’s data center revenue next year. Referencing the new export controls, Kress said that the backlog of demand for advanced chips like Vera Rubin means the rules would have no impact on the company’s top-line revenue.

In the long term, the company may face the loss of potential customers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia. Critics of Nvidia’s dependence on China claim that as much as 20% of its revenue comes from demand linked to the country — annual revenue at its Singapore subsidiary hit $104 billion in 2025 before Nvidia stopped disclosing those figures — but that’s clearly going to change.

Even before Nvidia decided to stop shipping H200s, China had largely refused to accept their delivery. The government would prefer to generate demand for the country’s domestic chip industry, even if major AI compute users want the still-superior Nvidia equipment, according to Jacob Feldgoise, a researcher at Georgetown’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology.

Meanwhile,Chinese frontier labs are finding ways to access Nvidia chips elsewhere. All of China’s leading AI models show evidence of having been trained on Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips that are prohibited from being exported to China.

That training may have taken place at data centers outside of China, but sales to those facilities will be barred under the new rules. If large data centers suited for training AI models want to buy Nvidia chips, they will have to certify they aren’t serving any Chinese customers, export control attorney Dan Fisher-Owens told TechCrunch.
If they can’t provide that certification, the new rules may force them toward other chip options and further eat into Nvidia’s market share.

articles.headline: Wales' Nations League campaign boosts Bellamy's belief despite loss to Portugal
keyFacts: Wales finished bottom of their Nations League group after a 3-2 loss to Portugal.
Manager Craig Bellamy stated that the team gained belief and proved they can compete at the highest level despite the results.
Wales will play a two-leg relegation play-off in March to determine if they remain in the top tier.
body: - Published
Craig Bellamy kept coming back to one word. Belief.
His Wales side had just lost a fifth game out of six to finish bottom of their Nations League group. Bellamy would have been forgiven for feeling a little bruised.
But there are ways of losing and ways of finishing bottom.
Wales were fearless against Portugal, exhilarating in attack and proving they can compete at the highest level of this competition, even as they were beaten 3-2 in Cardiff.

And while they were already consigned to the foot of the Group A4 table, Wales' previous performances mean they at least have the back-up of a relegation play-off in March to preserve their top-flight status.
"Belief's the biggest one," Bellamy said when he was asked what he and his team had taken from this campaign.
"Not just this game, but in general. We are beyond close to this level. We can more than compete at this level.
"We demand and want to expect to be. Getting into League A is big for us, but also staying in A is going to allow us to develop.
"You can only develop and improve by playing the best teams, and I felt we've taken another shift."
Wales have certainly fared better than they did when they were last in the top tier of the Nations League, when they finished with one point from six games and were relegated.
Victory against World Cup quarter-finalists Norway last month was their first at this level and, had they been more clinical in Oslo on Saturday, they might have got a second win of the campaign.
Ultimately, Wales' inability to take their chances â combined with sloppy defensive mistakes â meant their results did not match their performances.
And the reality is that they were up against stellar opposition, whose vastly superior resources showed with their greater ruthlessness at both ends of the pitch.
"If there's anything you would have learned from these games, then you see killers. That's why they're at the top," Bellamy added.

"I know people look at results. I'm fully aware of the business. This is all I know. But I think when you look at reality as well, and you look at our performances during this group, I couldn't ask for more.
"I feel we're closer than probably maybe the players thought they were. It's fine margins.
"But I feel the biggest word out of this now has been belief, really, for me."
Relegation play-off awaits in March
Wales had the best record of the four teams who finished bottom of their top-flight groups, meaning they have a second chance to avoid relegation in the form of a two-leg play-off in March.

At Friday's draw in Switzerland, Bellamy's side will discover whether they will face Slovenia, Hungary, Republic of Ireland or Bosnia-Herzegovina, who beat them in a World Cup play-off earlier this year.
Those teams all finished second in their League B groups and, as the League A team, Wales will have home advantage in the second leg.

"Going into the next one, we have to be in this group," said Bellamy. "If we want to develop as a football nation and keep going forward, we have to be playing against the best teams. It's only going to improve you.
"I know we can go back to League B... It's about playing the best teams. That's how we're going to get better. I honestly believe it."
Bellamy, who has a contract running to 2028, said: "I won't be here for the next Nations League. I won't be the manager then. So I'm doing it for the next one, but I'm also doing it for the players.
"We've got to. That's how we're going to be the best version of us and keep improving."

articles.headline: 'Oil wells that never run dry': Syntholene's CEO says one geothermal borehole can make unlimited jet fuel — but the company's Iceland plant has only made hydrogen so far
keyFacts: Syntholene CEO Dan Sutton claimed on X that a single geothermal well can supply unlimited fuel forever.
The startup's Iceland demonstration plant has produced hydrogen and passed an Imperial College review, but has not yet made synthetic fuel.
Future milestones for Syntholene include producing synthetic kerosene, naming a carbon source, and securing a binding commercial contract.
body: - Syntholene CEO Dan Sutton claims a single 10MW geothermal well equals about 200 football fields of desert solar and can feed "unlimited fuel, forever"
- Syntholene's Iceland demo has produced hydrogen and passed a company-funded Imperial College review, but has not produced synthetic fuel, and the review gave no costs
- The company has not named its carbon source, and its biggest customer link, Icelandair, is a non-binding letter conditional on scale and price
Dan Sutton, cofounder and CEO of the Canadian-listed synthetic fuel startup Syntholene, has a big claim for a single, albeit massive, hole in the ground.

In a post on X, he shared a clip of what he called a 10MW geothermal borehole and said it matches roughly 200 football fields of solar panels in the world's sunniest desert, plus another five fields of batteries to keep the output steady.

Sutton added that the well could deliver baseload energy for more than a century if well maintained, and that Syntholene's process is designed to turn wells like it into "low-cost oil wells that never run dry," signing off with the statement that "This is how we make unlimited fuel. Forever."
The math checks out, but the reading might be overwhelmingly optimistic

The post lands less than a month after Syntholene published a paid independent review of its demonstration plant in Iceland, and it is worth considering the message on its merits, with scrutiny in tow, as a message from the CEO of a company whose most recent private placement raised about $2.3 million at $0.45 per unit.
Some of the claims hold up better than one might be expected, but the most important one, the part where the geothermal well becomes an oil well, has not been demonstrated yet.
For starters, the post does not mention whether it is considering the 10MW mentioned as electricity or heat, a distinction that matters considerably when doing the math.

A 10MW electrical well running at a 90% capacity factor would produce about 79GWh a year. That capacity factor is realistic for mature geothermal: Calpine's 2025 figures for The Geysers in California show 5,471,562 net MWh generated in 2024 from a maximum capacity of 694 net MW, which works out to roughly 90%.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!

The most cited US data on solar land use, from NREL's 2013 study, found that generation-weighted solar plants need about 3.5 acres per GWh per year on average, and large fixed-tilt PV around 2.8 acres. That puts the solar equivalent at roughly 220 to 276 acres.

A US football field including end zones covers about 1.32 acres, so the range is about 167 to 209 fields. This means that Sutton's "~200" is fair on decade-old data, but newer, more efficient panels in a very sunny desert could pull it substantially lower.

If the 10MW is thermal, the comparison falls apart, because turning moderate-temperature geothermal heat into electricity loses most of the energy along the way. For the math to hold, the conversion would have to be electric. This does not change the fact that a 10MW well would be a relative outlier. A simple search shows that a single commercial geothermal production well typically generates 3 to 5 megawatts (MW) of net electrical power.

Fervo Energy, whose Nevada geothermal project for Google TechRadar Pro covered when it came online, provides a sobering benchmark too: its Project Red pilot supported about 3.5 MWe at peak in a 2023 test, but averaged 2.1 MWe gross and roughly 1.4 MWe net across more than 614 production days.

The 100-year claim is not absurd on face value: The same Calpine document above shows that a well drilled in 1955 is still producing at The Geysers today. The field around it tells a more complicated story. In its prime, The Geysers delivered 2GW of power, but productivity declined faster as multiple operators tapped the same connected reservoir, forcing operators to inject extra water to slow the slide.

Calpine, which runs most of the plants there, reported a 2024 maximum of 694 net MW across its share of the field. The field did not run out of heat. It ran short of the fluid and pressure that carry the heat to the surface, which is exactly the kind of maintenance problem that the "if well maintained" caveat quietly covers in the X post.

The "as long as the earth's mantle is hot" line also overreaches. Geothermal wells tap heat in the Earth's crust, which comes from the planet's formation and from radioactive decay, and any single reservoir can be drawn down faster than it recovers. Even large, well-known geothermal regions have hard limits: TechRadar reported earlier this year that the first 100MW phase of Microsoft's planned Kenya data center was already straining Olkaria's geothermal output.

Syntholene's demonstration facility sits at the historic Húsavík power station in northern Iceland, home to a 2MW Kalina-cycle geothermal plant commissioned in 2000 and fed by 120C brine from wells about 20 kilometers south of town. The company finished construction on June 22, about six months ahead of schedule, and the facility makes hydrogen, which the company describes as the principal feedstock for its fuel. It announced its first 500 kilograms of hydrogen on July 7 2026.
Validated but with caveats

Validation of the approach came on October 20 2026, when Syntholene released a review by Professor Nigel Brandon of Imperial College London. It concluded that the plant had achieved proof-of-performance for its geothermally integrated solid oxide electrolyzer, with average stack consumption of 34.90kWh per kilogram of hydrogen, equal to about 95.5% electrical efficiency, and 38.60kWh/kg for the system excluding steam generation.

The release is unusually candid about the limits, and they are significant: Hydrogen output was calculated from electrical current assuming 100% Faradaic efficiency rather than measured with a flow meter.

The efficiency figure excludes thermal inputs, steam generation, and geothermal circulation, so the 95% number omits the heat that makes the design work and cannot be compared directly with conventional electrolyzers. The review relied on company-supplied data and a virtual, not in-person, inspection.

Producing synthetic fuel is another challenge: a hydrocarbon needs carbon as well as hydrogen. Syntholene's website says its carbon feedstock is captured directly from point-source emissions, without naming the source, and Sutton told Proactive that using captured carbon means the company approaches carbon neutrality.

That matters for the "long after crude oil" promise. If the CO2 comes from a fossil-fueled emitter, Syntholene's endless fuel depends on someone still burning fossil fuels. It matters for regulation too. Under EU rules, captured industrial CO2 only counts toward renewable fuel credits if it is built into fuel before 2036 for power plant emissions, or 2041 for other industries. After that, only CO2 from the air or from biogenic and geological sources qualifies.

For now, Syntholene has quickly built a working, geothermally integrated electrolyzer, published its reviewer's caveats and fee, and Sutton's land-use comparison is roughly right if his megawatts are electric.

But "unlimited fuel, forever" describes a plant that simply does not exist yet. The milestones that would make the claim credible are the first synthetic kerosene from its demonstration facility at Húsavík, a named and eligible carbon source, and a binding offtake contract with an attached price.

articles.headline: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026, plus more AI workplace updates
keyFacts: CEO Satya Nadella announced Copilot Workspaces and an autonomous agent named Autopilot during the Microsoft Ignite conference keynote on Tuesday.
Microsoft introduced productivity tools including Today and Home to streamline workflows, alongside new AI features designed to improve workplace collaboration.
Microsoft launched Agent 365 Business Analytics and Cost Management tools to help enterprises track AI spending and measure return on investment.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- Microsoft Ignite is underway this week, focusing on enterprise AI updates.
- The company announced Copilot Workspaces, in line with other AI companies.
- New productivity and ROI features are also available today.
AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.
During the keynote for the company’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella announced Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.
More from ZDNET

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several new Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.
A Dot-like personal agent

Microsoft also announced Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft said, and assign it tasks.
Microsoft said the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

“Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft said.
The company added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.
Designing AI for work

Nadella also announced a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Currently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up quickly,” Microsoft said of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Microsoft also announced that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.
Tools to track ROI
While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can quickly rack up costs when unsupervised.
Microsoft announced a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Agent 365, which Microsoft announced last year, is the company’s observability platform. Microsoft said Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft showed how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

“It starts with a new way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft said. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”
Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

“Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft said. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise plans.

articles.headline: College basketball picks, schedule: Predictions for Duke vs. Illinois and more Top 25 games on Tuesday
keyFacts: Thirteen teams in the AP Top 25 poll will play on Tuesday, featuring marquee matchups like No. 5 Duke against No. 10 Illinois.
CBS Sports reported that No. 10 Illinois will face No. 5 Duke while missing key players due to injuries.
CBS Sports provided expert analysis and predictions for several top college basketball games scheduled for Tuesday.
body: Thirteen of the teams ranked in this week's AP Top 25 poll will be in action on Tuesday. The slate includes two marquee ranked-on-ranked matchups between No. 5 Duke and No. 10 Illinois and No. 2 Michigan State facing No. 14 Tennessee on the road. The opening day of the Players Era 8 tournament also begins in Las Vegas.

Duke and Illinois suffered their first losses to Michigan State and Texas Tech, respectively, last week. Now, they will face each other in one of the best nonconference games of the 2026-27 season. The Fighting Illini are still without preseason All-American David Mirkovic, while the Blue Devils are set to be at full strength at home.

Michigan State's wire-to-wire win over the Blue Devils in last week's Champions Classic was the most impressive result of the young season. Now, Tom Izzo's Spartans will be tested inside a hostile environment at Food City Center in Knoxville. Tennessee is off to a 3-0 start but hasn't quite lived up to its preseason top-10 ranking.

Another game on the schedule worth watching will see No. 20 Arkansas face Indiana at Madison Square Garden. Indiana enters this game 4-0 after wins over Syracuse and Tennessee Tech last week, while the Razorbacks have won back-to-back games since suffering their first loss of the season against Virginia earlier this month.
Let's dive into picks, predictions and expert analysis for this loaded Tuesday college basketball slate.
All times ET
No. 10 Illinois at No. 5 Duke

7 p.m. on ESPN, fuboTV (try for free): Illinois may have the No. 10 label, but this is not the roster of the 10th-best team in America. Starting wing Jake Davis, a 40% sharpshooter, is out with a long-term shoulder injury. All-American forward David Mirkovic (broken foot and appendectomy) will also miss this one. Illinois now has to walk into Cameron with three freshmen in the starting lineup, including two (Ethan Brown and Lincoln Williams), who no one knew a month ago. This is a young team that has had real trouble getting stops and rebounds. Now, it has to face supersized Duke without Davis and Mirkovic, two of the best rebounders on the team. The Blue Devils should be licking their chops after small-but-mighty Texas Tech ripped down 18 offensive rebounds against the Illini.

Illinois' awesome offense will have to put up a big number against Duke to stay in the game. That's easier said than done because Duke doesn't have many individual defenders to pick at. Dame Sarr, John Blackwell and Cayden Boozer are all good (or great) defenders on the perimeter. Duke is also huge up front with Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje and Pat Ngongba. Illinois will try to run Duke's bigs to death and use elite spacing to give lottery pick Quentin Coleman and slick-slashing wing Andrej Stojakovic room to shred. They'll make Boumtje Boumtje defend in space, but without splashing 10+ 3-pointers, it's hard to envision Illinois winning this one. Duke is healthier, deeper and more talented right now. I think Duke bounces back in a real way after the Michigan State debacle and gets back to playing the right way. Pick: Duke -7.5 -- Isaac Trotter
No. 19 Arkansas vs. Indiana

7:30 p.m. on Peacock: Arkansas entered this season with a very talented, but inexperienced roster. The returns over the first four games back are backing that claim. The Razorbacks still haven't played an "A" game yet. This is when it could happen against a very good Indiana team.

Five-star Arkansas guard Jordan Smith Jr. still hasn't had a game that announces himself as one of the elite players in this class. Arkansas coach John Calipari pretty much called his team out after an ugly win over Central Arkansas last week. How will his team respond? How about by beating one of the best nonconference opponents on its schedule? I'll take Arkansas to win. Pick: Arkansas -2.5 -- CS
No. 2 Michigan State at No. 14 Tennessee

9 p.m. on ESPN, fuboTV (try for free): If you're into spots, this is an all-Vols spot. Tennessee is fresh off an uninspiring five-point win over Tennessee State. Things couldn't be better for Michigan State after plastering Duke last week. And yet, the line is hovering around a possession. The X's and O's matter, too. To beat Michigan State's strong gap-help scheme, you need plenty of shooting. Tennessee has just that in Terrence Hill, Tyler Lundblade, Dai Dai Ames and Juke Harris, who are each capable of drilling three or four triples a night. Michigan State could also hold out breakout sophomore wing Jordan Scott, who is battling a balky shoulder injury. Tennessee's biggest issue so far has been a pretty iffy frontcourt, but Michigan State's front line isn't the most imposing unit to truly pour salt into that wound. I'm not bullish on Tennessee's long-term outlook, but this is a game it finds a way to win on its home floor as long as it keeps Jeremy Fears Jr. from taking 16 free throws. Pick: Tennessee +3.5 -- IT
Auburn vs. West Virginia

Midnight, Wednesday on ESPN, fuboTV (try for free): These two teams are built very similarly. Both have quick guards who can really score. Both have reliable role players. Both have a stable of bigs who can play. Auburn lost to Arizona by 11, but it was pretty impressive for long stretches of that game. Auburn's size gave Arizona real issues. I think it can do the same in this one against a West Virginia frontcourt that's solid but not quite on that level. WVU freshman guard Miles Sadler is going to be a heckuva player, but this is the first test that really matters for West Virginia. Getting a brawl against Arizona under its belt should help Auburn in this one. With everything being pretty close to equal, I'll lean on the team with better bigs. That's Auburn by the slimmest of margins. Pick: Auburn -1.5 -- IT
No. 1 Florida vs. Notre Dame

4:30 p.m., Players Era 8 in Las Vegas on ESPN, fuboTV (try for free): Florida has already been tested twice this season against Miami (neutral site) and Florida State (true road game). Now, the Gators hit the road again for a very intriguing showdown against Notre Dame — a team that is off to a surprising 4-0 start. Florida ranks top 10 in both offensive and defensive efficiency, per KenPom. The tape tells the same story. Florida can beat teams with its size and physicality. Florida grabs a ton of offensive rebounds and doesn't allow second-chance buckets.

How Notre Dame can pull an upset — and where the Fighting Irish do have the edge — is 3-point shooting. As a team, Notre Dame is shooting a sizzling 47.8% from beyond the arc. I do think this game has the potential to be closer than people think, but I'm still taking Florida to cover the double-digit spread. Pick: Florida -14 -- Cameron Salerno

articles.headline: House Democrats push to ban stock trading through rules package
keyFacts: House Democrats are pushing to ban congressional stock trading through the next House rules package, according to the report.
Representative-elect Sam Forstag stated that a ban should apply to both members and their families as a rule and legislation.
The House rules package is scheduled to be voted on in January after the speaker election.
body: Democrats are pushing to add a ban on congressional stock trading as part of the next rules package.

Reps.-elect Sam Forstag (D-MT) and Zach Dembo (D-KY), centrist Democrats who flipped red-leaning districts, as well as progressive Rep.-elect Brad Lander (D-NY), advocated the ban as part of the House rules, set to be voted on in January after the speaker election.

“We need to pass a real ban on stock trading here in Congress for not only members but for their family as well. We should be pushing this not only as legislation but as a rule, so that we get it done as quickly as possible,” said Forstag.
They also want to see a stock trade ban passed through the legislative process.
The push from Democrats across the ideological spectrum comes as the caucus debates the set of rules that will govern House business next year.
Rep. Jason Crow (D-CO), a vocal stock trade ban proponent, told the Washington Examiner that he will “absolutely” be advocating adding it as a rule.

“I’ve long said that we have to walk the talk, and there are things we can do that don’t require legislation,” Crow said. “It’ll take longer for us to get legislation passed, but until then, Americans desperately want to see that we’re willing to just immediately walk the talk and abide by the rules that we want to pass via legislation.”
When asked if he would raise the matter ahead of caucus leadership elections on Wednesday, Crow said “people running for leadership know where I stand.”
HOW HOUSE RULES COULD LOOK DIFFERENT IN A DEMOCRATIC CONGRESS
This would be the latest rule floated by Democrats as they decide what rules package they want to put on the House floor in January.
Other rules changes floated for consideration by Democrats have been term limits for committee chairs and allowing proxy voting for members who are expectant mothers and new parents.

articles.headline: White House blasts 'Trumpcare for All' pitch from far-left El-Sayed who called president 'unserious fool'
keyFacts: Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed urged President Donald Trump in a video to support a universal healthcare plan called 'Trumpcare for All.'
A White House spokeswoman rejected the proposal, stating that government-run healthcare would harm existing coverage and increase federal deficits.
Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed is scheduled to take office on January 3, 2027.
body: The White House blasted far-left Michigan Democrat Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed's pitch to President Donald Trump to embrace "Trumpcare for All," warning that the Medicare for All proposal would threaten Americans' existing health coverage.

"The Radical Democrats’ socialist proposal for a government takeover of healthcare should really be called ‘Medicare for None’ as it destroys access to the life-saving care Americans rely on daily," White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster told Fox News Digital.
The sharp response came after El-Sayed , who recently called Trump an "unserious fool," posted a 16-second video Tuesday urging the president to embrace the progressive proposal.
BERNIE SANDERS THINKS MEDICARE FOR ALL BILL COULD PASS, 'NOT ABSOLUTELY CERTAIN' TRUMP WOULD VETO

"I think there is a responsibility that we have to engage with [Trump] as the unserious fool that he is," El-Sayed said during a recent appearance on "Pod Save America," according to earlier Fox News Digital reporting.
Despite those remarks, the senator-elect struck a more conciliatory tone in his latest appeal.
"Donald. Habibi. Midterms were rough. I get it," El-Sayed said in the video posted Nov. 17, addressing Trump with the Arabic term "habibi," commonly translated as "my dear" or "my beloved."
"Trumpcare for All. It's really popular. People really want healthcare. You can put your name all over it."
EL-SAYED ADMITS FREE HEALTHCARE MEANS PAYING 'A LITTLE BIT MORE IN TAXES' REGARDLESS OF INCOME

The video featured a mock "Trumpcare" card and an AI-generated image depicting Trump as Jesus Christ, which El-Sayed, a Muslim, referenced while urging the president to embrace socialized, taxpayer-funded healthcare.
"Donald, this is your chance to heal the sick (like in that one AI image. You know the one)," El-Sayed said.
The White House instead pointed to Trump's efforts to lower prescription drug prices , contrasting those policies with the single-payer system advocated by El-Sayed.

"President Trump is focused on taking on the special interests that are driving up the costs of healthcare for all Americans including through his historic efforts to ensure American patients never pay more than those in other developed nations for all prescription drugs, which has already saved Americans well over $1 Billion," Schuster said.
MAJORITY OF AMERICANS BROADLY REJECT SOCIALIST IDEOLOGY EVEN AS FAR LEFT SURGES TO POWER

"The President will continue delivering real results that lower costs and put Americans first, while Democrats push ideas that have devastated economies and ruined healthcare quality anywhere they have been implemented."

The administration also cited a U.S. Council of Economic Advisers' analysis estimating that Medicare for All would increase the federal budget deficit by approximately $47.4 trillion between 2027 and 2036 in the absence of additional taxes or revenues.
The White House also cited a CEA projection that Medicare for All would shift large numbers of Americans away from employer-sponsored insurance and into a new government-run coverage system.

Medicare for All, a sweeping single-payer health care proposal championed by Democratic socialists , would replace much of the nation's private health insurance system with federally financed coverage. Supporters argue it would guarantee coverage, while critics warn of substantial tax increases and massive federal spending.
El-Sayed's public appeal was not his first attempt to recruit Trump to the idea.
During a CNN appearance earlier this month, the incoming senator suggested that the president could attach his name to a universal health care proposal.
"Donald, if you're watching, we can put your name on it. I know you like to put your name on stuff," El-Sayed said, according to a Nov. 10 social media post by CNN anchor Kaitlan Collins.
The unusual overture follows a contentious Michigan Senate race in which El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers.

The Democrat also mocked Trump, Vice President JD Vance and Rogers during his election victory remarks , adding to the contrast between his earlier criticism of the administration and his latest invitation to collaborate.
El-Sayed is scheduled to take office Jan. 3, 2027.
El-Sayed's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.
Fox News Digital's Leo Briceno contributed to this reporting.

articles.headline: Trump brushes off NSA internal network outage: ‘it’s like that when you’re big and powerful’ – live
keyFacts: Donald Trump brushed off reports of an NSA internal network outage, which an agency spokesperson said was scheduled routine maintenance.
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said recent tech outages across multiple sectors were likely caused by system upgrades rather than cyberattacks.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the FBI is assisting an investigation into a malfunctioning router that previously caused thousands of flight groundings.
body: Trump brushes off reports of NSA internal network outage: 'it's fine'
Donald Trump brushed off reports that the National Security Agency’s internal network is down in remarks to reporters in Manila today, saying “it’s fine.”
“It’s like when you’re big and powerful, and you have all the money. Things like that happen. It’s fine,” Trump said.
As we reported earlier, an NSA spokesperson told the Guardian the outage was the result of “scheduled routine maintenance.”
But after a series of high profile outages over the past week – affecting banks, air traffic control, United Airlines and Microsoft – some have begun to raise concerns.
“If this is all a coincidence, it’s like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world,” Republican senator Josh Hawley told reporters today.

The Board of Peace, which is overseeing the US-brokered ceasefire in Gaza, told the United Nations Security Council today that the ceasefire will collapse if steps are not taken to uphold the full peace agreement.

“The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains the principal risk to the process,” says the report, a copy of which was obtained by The Associated Press.

It adds, “Restrictions imposed by Israel on the entry of supplies and equipment, compounded by funding shortfalls, continued to impede preparedness and response efforts,” calling for immediate “scaled-up entry of shelter and winterization materials.”
The Board delivered its first report to the United Nations in May, at which time it warned: “A ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely.”
Defense secretary Pete Hegseth said the Pentagon “will pass a full, clean audit by 2028” in response to news that the defense department failed a financial audit for the ninth year in a row.

The Defense Department was first audited in 2018 and given 10 years to pass an annual audit. An inspector general report released yesterday showed the agency had failed audit again for fiscal year 2026. The news comes as the Trump administration is seeking a record $1.5tn for defense spending.
Despite failing the audit, Hegseth wrote in a social media post: “We are more than halfway there – huge, historic progress so far.”

As defense department CFO Jules Hurst told Reuters, a majority of the Pentagon’s units passed audit for the first time. According to Hurst, 14 of the Pentagon’s 25 stand-alone reporting entities passed audit in the 2026 fiscal year, up from 11 the prior year.
Donald Trump has been granted a temporary delay before he must give a witness statement in his $10bn defamation lawsuit against the BBC.
In late October, a federal magistrate judge ordered Trump to sit for a deposition by BBC lawyers by 11 December. But on Tuesday, a federal district court judge extended the deadline until 22 January.
Lisa Cook, the Federal Reserve governor that Donald Trump has sought to fire since August 2025, has declined to appear before a Trump administration committee next month.
Cook’s attorneys declined the appearance, saying the committee considering whether she should be fired is committed to a predetermined outcome.

“Governor Cook has no legal obligation to participate in an unfair hearing – and indeed, has a duty to the Federal Reserve to decline to participate in any proceeding that would undermine the institution’s unique status and independence,” Abbe David Lowell, Cook’s lawyer, wrote in a letter released Tuesday to White House counsel William Scharf.

Health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, a longtime vaccine skeptic, said the United States will work to regain measles elimination status and blamed “worldwide COVID-era disruptions” for interrupting routine childhood vacccination.

“Worldwide COVID-era disruptions interrupted routine childhood vaccination, leaving gaps in protection here and abroad. The multi-year global outbreak has caused many nations to lose their elimination status including, Armenia, Austria, Azerbaijan, Bolivia, Canada, Mexico, Spain, United Kingdom, and Uzbekistan,” Kennedy said in a social media post.

Kennedy – who has overseen the Centers for Disease Control losing up to one-third of its staff, interfered in the agency’s reporting of measles deaths and has spread misinformation about the measles vaccines – added, “I continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles.”

The second Trump administration also made broad changes that challenge measles elimination globally. Some of Trump’s first acts in 2024 included withdrawal from the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Global Vaccine Alliance (GAVI). GAVI provides measles vaccines to nations such as India and Malawi. There are about 95,000 measles deaths globally, according to the World Health Organization, mostly in unvaccinated children under five years old.
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told Fox Business that a recent string of tech outages are likely due to system upgrades and not a cyber attack.

“Everybody recognizes it’s time to upgrade their systems, and as they upgrade them, they’re not coming back as expected in all cases, and in some cases, systems have to hand off to other systems, and those handoffs are not coming back as expected,” Clayton told the Claman Countdown program on Fox Business today.
He added, “Looking very diligently across the landscape, we are not seeing this as a cyber attack incident.”

Apple reported three outages today, amid a rash of high profile outages in recent days affecting government and private companies. Users are also reporting outages at Marriott International, the largest hotel operator in the US, the Associated Press reports.

Apple reported that its Apple Music, App Store and AppleCare services experienced full outages today. “Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning,” the company said in an emailed statement to the AP. “We’re working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible.”
The AP also noted that users posting on Reddit and Downdetector.com reported that Marriott was experiencing an outage. The hotel chain did not immediately respond to an email inquiry from the AP.

Markwayne Mulline, the homeland security secretary, defended his decision to fly to a college football game on Saturday by private government plane, as Americans weathered widespread flight delays and cancellations.
In an interview with CNBC the former Oklahoma senator said, “We still got to live our life.”
Mullin traveled on a government aircraft on Saturday to watch a football game between Louisiana State University and the University of Texas, the New York Post reported on Tuesday.
Trump brushes off reports of NSA internal network outage: 'it's fine'
Donald Trump brushed off reports that the National Security Agency’s internal network is down in remarks to reporters in Manila today, saying “it’s fine.”
“It’s like when you’re big and powerful, and you have all the money. Things like that happen. It’s fine,” Trump said.
As we reported earlier, an NSA spokesperson told the Guardian the outage was the result of “scheduled routine maintenance.”
But after a series of high profile outages over the past week – affecting banks, air traffic control, United Airlines and Microsoft – some have begun to raise concerns.
“If this is all a coincidence, it’s like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world,” Republican senator Josh Hawley told reporters today.

The outage of a highly classified internal network at the National Security Agency (NSA), was the result of “scheduled routine maintenance,” an NSA spokesperson told the Guardian in a statement. NSA Net, the network that allows the agency’s employees to send classified information internally, was down today, according to several reports. While sources sources told CNN that there was no evidence of a cyber-attack, it is the latest disruption in a series of outages over the last week that have affected the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Microsoft, Chase Bank and JP Morgan.

Chuck Schumer again insisted today that he has the votes to secure the leadership position when Democrats take the majority in the new year. “I’m confident I’ll be the next leader, I have the votes, and we’re all going to roll up our sleeves, and we are going to focus on lowering costs, ending corruption. Those are the things we’re focused on,” he said, without addressing what the challenge from Senator Chris Van Hollen, a progressive, says about faith in Schumer’s leadership. “We are all united together,” Schumer said, despite the fact that several members of the caucus have pledged support for Van Hollen.

Sean Duffy, the transportation secretary, saidhe’s making “a nice ask” for an additional $50bn in funding for air safety upgrades following the nationwide ground-stop of thousands of flights last week. Several Democrats have slammed the request, arguing that the Republicans guaranteed a $12.5bn air traffic control package last year, and only $1bn has been spent and $8bn has yet to be obligated.

Duffy also said today the FBI is now assisting the investigation into the newly-installed router responsible for the grounding. However, he told reporters today that the US intelligence agencies have assured him the issues were not the result of a cyber-attack. “I think it’s important that we have all precautions. So I asked Kash [Patel] to send me part of his FBI team to be part of the analyzing of this router,” Duffy said.

Hung Cao, who currently serves as the acting Navy secretary, faced lawmakers on the Senate armed services committee to be confirmed as the branch’s permanent top official. During his hearing today, Cao said the eight suicide attempts on board the USS Abraham Lincoln – during a record-breaking deployment– were actually “suicide mitigations”, and defended conditions on the warship. More here and here
Jensen Huang, the embattled former CEO of Nvidia, will appear before House lawmakers on three key committees on 1 December. Huang will appear alongside Nvidia’s general counsel Tim Teter.

Meanwhile, two departments have confirmed they are investigating computing company Megaspeed, suspecting it of violating US export controls by helping to ship tech giant Nvidia’s chips to China. A joint statement issued by the Department of Commerce and the Department of Justice explains that Megaspeed has been under investigation since 2024, for “potential export control violations.”

Earlier, in Manila, Donald Trump said that US authorities take “very seriously” any possible threat to Washington, following reports Iran was planning to target officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb. “If there is [such a threat], they will pay a price the likes of which no other country has ever paid before,” the president said. “I hope it’s not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy.”
Duffy says nationwide grounding was not result of a cyber hack but FBI is assisting investigation into router malfunction
Sean Duffy said today that the US intelligence agencies have assured him the decision to ground of all thousands of flights last week was not the result of a cyber-attack.
However, the FBI is now assisting the investigation into the newly-installed router responsible for the malfunction.

“I think it’s important that we have all precautions. So I asked Kash [Patel] to send me part of his FBI team to be part of the analyzing of this router,” Duffy said. “If we were subject to a hack, we will share that with you as well, but all of my intelligence partners are telling me that wasn’t the case. But again, we have the FBI there partnering with us as we work through this analysis.”
Duffy noted today that he’s making “a nice ask” for an additional $50bn in funding for air safety upgrades, but said he would wait and see how Congress works to allocate the funding.

“Whether it’s on a party line vote or if it’s a bipartisan vote, I do think this is this is one moment in a very charged political environment … where almost all Americans and bipartisan members of both bodies are kind of in agreement that we should lean in and do it. So how they do their work, we’ll watch that together,” he told reporters today.

articles.headline: San Diego dumps both Flock cameras and smart streetlights
keyFacts: San Diego city council voted to end surveillance contracts with vendors Flock and Ubicquia on Monday.
Advocates celebrated the political victory after building a diverse coalition of critics against the technology.
Mayor Todd Gloria stated he respects the decision and will not veto the halt of camera operations.
body: On Monday evening, San Diego’s city council voted to end its contracts with two surveillance equipment vendors, Flock and Ubicquia. San Diego is one of the largest cities to end its relationship with Flock, the startup with an estimated valuation of $8.3 billion.
“We fucking won!” Lily Irani of the Transparent and Responsible Use of Surveillance Technology (TRUST) SD Coalition told Ars.
She and her colleagues have been among the loudest critics in recent years.

“The national energy creating left and right and center coalitions was the major cause [of the political victory],” she said, noting that it was only last month that one of the councilmembers revoked his support, creating an opening for a political majority to halt the surveillance.
That council member, Stephen Whitburn, said in an October press conference that he wanted his fellow citizens to “feel safe.”
“If Flock cameras are causing many San Diegans to feel unsafe, then they have lost effectiveness as a public safety tool,” he said at the time.

After the Monday vote, San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria said in a social media post that he “respect[ed] the Council’s decision” and would not veto the move to stop operation of the cameras across the city.

Andrew Smith, a spokesperson for Flock, told Ars in an email on Tuesday that the company also “respect[s] the city’s decision.” But Flock isn’t happy about it. “When a tool that is actively helping solve violent crimes is removed, public safety moves backward,” Smith wrote. “That has real consequences: cases will take longer to solve, organized retail theft crews will operate with fewer obstacles, a missing child may not be returned home, and victims may wait longer, or indefinitely, for justice.”

articles.headline: Haitians protest in support of El Salvador’s anti-gang troop deployment
keyFacts: Demonstrators in several Haitian cities marched to support a troop deployment from El Salvador aimed at fighting local gangs.
El Salvador announced it will end its deployment of about 2,500 troops once four missing Salvadoran aviation technicians are found.
Haitian Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier expressed gratitude for the troop surge and urged the Salvadoran forces to stay.
body: Demonstrators have marched in several Haitian cities to show support for a deployment of troops from El Salvador, despite concerns that the outside intervention may worsen instability in the Caribbean country.
On Tuesday, hundreds of protesters rallied in the streets of cities like the capital, Port-au-Prince, bearing signs with slogans like “Down with the gangs”.

Haiti has long struggled with gang violence, but the crisis worsened around 2021, after the assassination of President Jovenel Moise. His death further weakened Haiti’s central government, and experts say gangs took advantage of the eroding public confidence to expand their influence.
The October 18 kidnapping of four Salvadoran aviation technicians near Port-au-Prince prompted El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele to respond with a military operation to Haiti.
But on Monday, El Salvador confirmed it would end its deployment of about 2,500 troops once the missing Salvadoran airmen were found.
“If they reappear tomorrow, as President Bukele said, we will leave,” Salvadoran Security Minister Gustavo Villatoro said.
That announcement, however, was followed by public gestures of support and diplomatic engagements, with some top officials in Haiti encouraging the Salvadoran deployment to stay.
Haitian Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier travelled to San Salvador on Monday and expressed gratitude for the troop surge.
“The Haitian people applaud the decision of Nayib Bukele to send troops,” Pelissier said on Monday.
He added that Haitian security forces, together with their international counterparts, had recently managed to regain control of Haiti’s national football stadium, held by gangs for years.
“During the operation, we discovered several human skulls inside the stadium,” Bukele claimed in a social media post last week.
A ‘mano dura’ approach

The timeline for the Salvadoran troop withdrawal is uncertain. While El Salvador has framed its deployment as a rescue mission, the leader of Haiti’s 400 Mawozo gang, Wilson Joseph, told The Associated Press that the four technicians are already dead.
Joseph added that the abduction took place in territory controlled by Chen Mechan, a rival gang. He provided no evidence to back his assertions.
Bukele, however, has championed his country’s role in confronting Haiti’s gangs, using social media to promote the offensive and sharing videos of military operations.
The Salvadoran president — who once referred to himself as the “world’s coolest dictator” — has been credited with popularising a “mano dura” or “strong hand” approach to regional security.
Faced with one of the highest homicide rates in the world, Bukele launched a hardline security crackdown on gangs in El Salvador in 2022, including mass arrests and mass trials.
His heavy-handed approach has led to a sharp decline in crime but has also been widely condemned for human rights abuses.
Critics have warned that transplanting such tactics to Haiti could spark a backlash, leading to greater instability and risks to civilians.
They have also criticised the lack of long-term planning for El Salvador’s troop deployment; a sudden withdrawal, for instance, could worsen the situation for Haiti’s security forces.
Bukele is campaigning for a third term in El Salvador’s February presidential election, and analysts speculate his actions in Haiti could be used as a campaign tool to drum up support.
A series of international actions
The Salvadoran deployment is the latest in a series of international interventions in Haiti.

Such foreign involvement is often controversial. The United States, for instance, has sent troops to Haiti on multiple occasions in the 20th century, occupying the country for decades and seizing control of its central bank.
More recently, a United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) arrived in Haiti in April, to help address the widespread gang violence.

Gangs control more than 80 percent of the capital region. The conflict has killed more than 22,000 people since 2022. UN reports attribute more than half of the deaths in the first nine months of the year to security operations, including the deaths of 300 civilians.
The UN also says almost 2,000 people have been displaced since the arrival of Salvadoran troops.
But Pelissier said Haiti’s government had not reported any civilian casualties in the latest operations, which he described as professional.
“The best to do is to avoid, as much as possible, human rights violations, and that’s what we are doing together,” the minister said.

articles.headline: Miami Heat shows off its 'Vice City hardwood' ahead of the big Grand Theft Auto 6 basketball game
keyFacts: The Miami Heat will play the Milwaukee Bucks on a Grand Theft Auto 6 themed court to promote the upcoming game.
The promotional basketball game is scheduled for November 18, one day before the official release of Grand Theft Auto 6.
Fans can watch the themed game live or via a broadcast on ESPN.
body: Grand Theft Auto 6 launches at midnight on November 19 in your local time zone, meaning that people in New Zealand will be playing it while I'm still stuck at work on November 18. Unless, that is, you do your gaming on a PC, in which case GTA 6 won't be launching at all—at least, not until some indeterminate span of time has passed and Take-Two Interactive deigns to bestow it upon us.

But that doesn't mean we can't indulge in all the pre-release hype, just like everyone else, and so here we are with a look at the "Vice City hardwood," upon which NBA team the Miami Heat—in the guise of the Vice City's hometown team—will square off against the Milwaukee Bucks.

It's an extensive overhaul, with a huge Vice City logo at center court, the VI logos in the paint, and the "I Heart Vice City" slogans at either end. Yeah, it's marketing, but I have to admit it looks pretty cool too.
And yes, there's a themed uniform too:

Renting an entire NBA team as a promotional tool really puts a finger on just how big Grand Theft Auto 6 is. GTA 5 was big, absolutely, but GTA 6 is huge: Take-Two is looking to make something in the neighborhood of $3.5 billion in GTA 6's launch quarter alone.

And it's not just the dollar signs that impress: GTA 6 is also being recognized as a mainstream cultural phenomenon in ways that previous games in the series never were, or could be. It's honestly kind of amazing how far things have come in the past 40+ years.

The Vice City-ified Miami Heat will face the Milwaukee Bucks on November 18, one day before the release of Grand Theft Auto 6. If you can't be there to see it live, the game will also be broadcast on ESPN.
