articles.headline: When do we start worrying about all these outages?
keyFacts: Recent widespread technical outages disrupted Microsoft 365, flights, banks, and other services, with no indication of malicious cyberattacks.
Microsoft said a flawed internal infrastructure update caused a day-long outage that disrupted widely used programs like Outlook, Word, and Excel.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated he cannot guarantee that the recent flight groundings will not occur again in the near future.
body: Have you tried to take a flight in the last week? What about check your email , your bank balance , your Apple account ? (Or, for a select few of us, your top-secret internal spy agency network ?)

If you have, you might have noticed that some or all of those services didn’t work as expected. First, Microsoft’s cloud programs, such as Outlook, went down late last week. Then, all of the planes were grounded on Friday. And this week, we had to deal with the bank outages, a separate United Airlines-specific outage, the Apple outage, and the NSA communications outage.

As of this writing, most of these issues have now been ironed out, at least for the time being, and there’s no indication that any of them were cyberattacks or otherwise malicious. But whatever the reasons, it sure feels like there have been a lot more outages this week and last than in a usual seven-day stretch.

To get to the bottom of it — hopefully before something else shorts out — the Today, Explained team spoke with Lily Hay Newman , a senior writer at WIRED who covers hacking, information security, and digital privacy.

She spoke with Today, Explained co-host Sean Rameswaram about why it took Microsoft so long to get Outlook back on its feet, all of the other recent outages we’ve suffered, and whether it’s as unprecedented as it feels in the moment. Plus, she explains how AI is causing a broader “vulnepocalypse” (or “ Vulnageddon ”), even if it’s not specifically the culprit of all of our current outages.

Below is an excerpt of Newman’s conversation with Sean, edited for length and clarity. There’s much more in the full podcast, so listen to Today, Explained wherever you get your podcasts, including Apple Podcasts , Pandora , and Spotify .

Lily, we spent the first half of the show talking about the issues with our air traffic control systems, but last week, of course, also brought chaos to a lot of people’s inboxes when Outlook was not so good. Tell us what happened there.

Microsoft 365, so all of the productivity platforms, had a massive outage and it dragged on for a full day, which is very noticeable when it’s a set of products that are as integrated in everything, as 365 is.
That means you just can’t work, right? This was probably billions of dollars of productivity lost.
Yeah, this is the cloud version of Microsoft Office: Outlook, Word, Excel, Copilot, Teams. If that’s your productivity platform, then yeah, you can’t work. That’s everything.
Microsoft is so enmeshed in the tech ecosystem, even before all of the cloud platforms, because they’re the Windows maker. They’re in everything.
What happened?

Microsoft, a few days later, on Monday, what they were saying was that they had sent out an update. It’s a Windows update, but it’s only really for their infrastructure. It’s not an update in consumer Windows. It’s not something your laptop would’ve gotten, but it has been out and proliferating through their infrastructure for about three months. But it actually had a flaw in it that wasn’t caught by their testing.

At the same time, they say cloud infrastructure is all about managing traffic and managing different regions of data centers. The issue with that three months of proliferation of that update started triggering and that’s why it was such an intractable issue.

At first, I saw it and I thought, okay, it’ll be a few hours, three hours or something, and they’ll fix it. And then, waking up Friday morning, it’s still not fixed. And it’s like, whoa, so something’s really going on.
And so it was the interplay of multiple factors that made it so hard for them to recover, they say.
Okay. Very different situations here between air traffic control and Microsoft 365. However, both kind of have a similar origin story in that they’re about patching systems and upgrading systems.
True, yes.
We’ve heard from Sean Duffy, Transportation secretary, that he cannot guarantee what happened on Friday won’t happen again in the near distant future.
Very ominous.
Have we heard something more reassuring from Microsoft?

Microsoft would definitely say, “This isn’t going to happen again. We want to give you all assurances. We are so sorry. Sometimes problems arise because of cyber attacks or exploitation of vulnerabilities.”
And then it’s kind of like, ‘Well, why weren’t all those systems patched? There was a patch out.’

But a lot of times patching is slower than we would like because the ramifications of a bad patch or an unforeseen consequence of an update can be really severe, and so organizations tend to be very nervous.

But it’s never the last time. These types of outages and failures happen in all technology systems and they will continue to, but people try to learn as much as they can from each incident and make things more and more robust.
Maybe a good time to ask you about all of the other breakdowns we’ve been having in our technology and elsewhere over the last few weeks.
I mean, people may not have even realized they just lived through something called Black October . What is Black October, beyond Halloween?

In October there were a few things going on, including with the widely used web scripting language, PHP. There were these two vulnerabilities in it that researchers were really concerned that if they were exploited, they could cause remote access takeovers of all different websites and all different platforms.
And so there was this big, industry-wide effort to make sure that everybody was patching — a “We have to patch this right away, don’t wait” type of thing.
So there’s Black October and then there’s the “vulnepocalypse.” People have been talking about this for maybe about a year now, this idea—
Everything’s vulnerable?
Right. Or that AI tools—
We need a better name for that.

Look, it’s not my thing. I’m just doing air quotes here, heavy air quotes. But this idea that agentic AI and AI models are becoming more and more powerful and adept at finding bugs in software and in helping both researchers and, potentially, attackers figure out how to exploit those vulnerabilities and weaponize them.

There’s this [idea] that cybersecurity is always this cat and mouse — again, I’m doing the air quotes — “cat and mouse game,” or an “arms race” is another phrase that’s often used. And so that in itself is not new, but the idea that AI in the mix just really accelerates it for both sides, and how to manage that dynamic.

Then there was this Iranian cyber attack on supermarket fridges or Binance getting hacked for, I don’t know, I think the most money I’ve ever heard about in any kind of hacker heist ever — $6 billion?
It was. Yeah.
I thought that we were meant to believe that crypto was unhackable, and here we are getting hacked for $6 billion?
I just want everyone to know you can rest easy. Things were already really bad before.

The fridge hacks, for example, the vulnerabilities that are being exploited there actually kind of go back numerous years. French officials have pointed to Iranian actors as having been behind at least some of those. This is targeting the food supply chain.
And same with the Binance situation. North Korean hackers stealing cryptocurrency, including large sums of cryptocurrency, is a story that reporters have been following for years and years and years.
And then on Monday, we had this bank outage across banks across the United States — Bank of America, Chase, Wells Fargo.
It just feels like everything’s breaking at a time where we’re on the precipice of driverless cars and AI running everything. Is it getting worse, or is it just a rough few months here?

To me, this stuff feels more cyclical. People may remember eight to 10 years ago when there were a ton of DDoS attacks taking down huge services. There was even basically an East Coast internet outage.

For me, it feels like we’re in another round of those, one of those moments where a lot of stuff starts to pile up and incident responders are really overworked and really exhausted and then other things are happening and nobody has as much elasticity or bandwidth because there’s so many things piling up at once — especially right now, in this new era of ubiquitous AI and access to more and more capable AI systems.
Again, it’s not to diminish that feeling. It’s just maybe helpful to have some context that it’s not truly, truly unprecedented right now.

articles.headline: Nvidia reports bumper results as firm says it's not reinstating Huang
keyFacts: Nvidia reported that quarterly sales doubled to $115.8bn and profits reached $65bn in its first results since the exit of founder Jensen Huang.
Nvidia chair Harvey Jones stated that the board does not intend to reinstate Huang, while interim chief executive Collette Kress assured investors it is business as usual.
Nvidia stated that revenue will rise another 13% in the next quarter, and board chair Harvey Jones said the company is searching for a permanent CEO.
body: - Published
Nvidia's quarterly sales doubled to top $100bn for the first time as the company insisted it is not reinstating ousted founder Jensen Huang.
In the company's first results since Huang's dramatic exit, interim chief executive Collette Kress said it is "business as usual" and told investors: "We've got this."
The company's quarterly sales doubled from a year earlier, reaching $115.8bn (Â£86.9bn), with shares in the company jumping 5% in after-hours trading.
Earlier on Tuesday, Huang said he would be "honoured" to return and lead Nvidia, having quit following two alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a possible spy for China.
"The board does not intend to reinstate him," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said during a Tuesday call with financial analysts.

The company's profits also doubled from a year ago. For the quarter, which covered the three months to October 25, profit hit $65bn. Its revenue from data centres, a significant part of Nvidia's business, also doubled to $107bn in the same time period.
Going forward, the company said its rapid growth is poised to continue, and revenue will rise another 13% in the next quarter.
Given the uncertainty surrounding the company after Huang's exit, financial analysts had been unsure Nvidia would provide any forward-looking guidance.

Daniela Hathorn, a senior analyst for trading platform Capital.com, said Nvidia's results "offer a strong answer to concerns that demand for AI infrastructure is cooling" and temper immediate worry that Huang was irreplaceable as a leader.

"The harder question is whether Nvidia can preserve the strategic advantage Huang helped build," Hathorn added. "His exit is unlikely to change orders already committed, but could matter more when Nvidia makes its next round of decisions on products, partnerships and investment."
Kress seemed eager to stress that Nvidia can continue to not only succeed, but lead the ongoing AI buildout happening throughout the technology industry.
"It is business as usual," she said of what is happening inside of Nvidia now. "Our partners, our suppliers, all of them are 100% behind us."
She added that Nvidia's leadership team has "stood up very strongly over the last week... working seamlessly in all of their departments and projects".

"Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed." Kress said before leaving the analyst call. "We've got this."

Despite board chairman Jones saying earlier that the company would not answer analyst questions about Huang or Nvidia's investigation into his conduct, he did address the search for a permanent replacement.
Jones said Nvidia is working with an executive search firm and is considering internal and external candidates, but that the company would not rush its selection.

"With the advanced technology and the national security dynamics in the marketplace, our new CEO will have to navigate those waters carefully," Jones said. "The search will be thorough and we want to do it as quickly as possible, but we won't do it before we find the exact right person."

articles.headline: Man charged in Peoria, Illinois ethanol plant bomb threat that forced mass evacuation
keyFacts: Andrew M. Kozak was indicted for allegedly emailing a bomb threat to a Peoria ethanol plant.
Authorities found an explosive device at the facility, which forced a mass evacuation of thousands of residents.
Kozak was arrested on Monday and was scheduled to make his initial federal court appearance on Tuesday afternoon.
body: A federal grand jury has indicted an Illinois man on charges that he emailed a bomb threat to an ethanol plant in Peoria last week. Authorities later found an explosive device at the plant and evacuated thousands of people within a 1-mile area.

Andrew M. Kozak, 41, of Chillicothe, Illinois, was charged with threats regarding explosives and transmitting a threat in interstate commerce, according to an indictment filed Tuesday in U.S. District Court in Peoria.

The indictment alleges that Kozak “sent an email to BioUrja which indicated that explosive devices had been placed at the BioUrja facility in Peoria.” The indictment alleges the email was sent on Nov. 13. The indictment does not accuse Kozak of actually planting a bomb, but authorities have said an explosive device was found at the ethanol plant.

“The FBI and its partners have been combing through evidence, serving legal process, conducting interviews and executing searches to identify this individual,” FBI Springfield Special Agent in Charge Ryan Presley said at a news conference Tuesday at the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Peoria.

Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives Assistant Special Agent in Charge John Maniff said Kozak’s arrest Monday morning, within 72 hours of the incident, resulted from a coordinated investigation involving federal, state, and local authorities. Kozak was arrested when he arrived at BioUrja.

The indictment does not give a motive, and other information in the case remains sealed. Authorities have not said why BioUrja was targeted. Officials also declined to say whether others were involved or how Kozak was identified and did not give details beyond the discovery of an explosive device at the plant on Friday. The FBI says the investigation remains active.

Kozak was scheduled to make his initial appearance in federal court in Peoria on Tuesday afternoon. No attorney was listed for Kozak on the federal court website. He remains in the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service .

If convicted, Kozak faces up to 10 years in prison on the explosives threat charge and up to five years on the email charge. Each count also carries a fine of up to $250,000 and up to three years of supervised release. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Darilynn J. Knauss and Assistant U.S. Attorney Douglas F. McMeyer are prosecuting the case. An indictment is merely an accusation, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

A LinkedIn profile matching Kozak’s name lists a process trainee job at BioUrja. “Learning how to operate an ethanol plant,” Kozak wrote under his job description. BioUrja has not confirmed whether Kozak worked there.

Kozak has a criminal record in Nebraska , where prison records show he served two years in prison on burglary charges in three counties. He was released in 2008. Kozak went back to prison in 2013 on a burglary charge in a fourth county and was released in 2014, records show.
Kozak allegedly planted the bomb on Friday, then sent a bomb threat to the company. Federal agents executed a search warrant at Kozak’s home in Chillicothe, about 15 miles north of Peoria.
The FBI’s Springfield office is now in charge of the investigation.

BioUrja notified Peoria police around 1:08 p.m. Central on Friday that it had received a bomb threat. Employees were in the building when the email arrived, Peoria Police Department Public Information Officer Semone Roth told the Washington Examiner . Police found a suspicious package at about 2 p.m., determined at about 6:45 p.m. that it posed a credible threat, and rendered it safe at about 9:12 p.m. No injuries were reported.

The evacuation order lasted about 18 hours and affected thousands of people. Peoria Police Chief Brad Dixon estimated about 2,500 homes were affected. The order was lifted around 1 p.m. on Saturday after searches found no additional devices. The zone covered parts of Downtown Peoria, much of the Southside and Warehouse District, and areas across the Illinois River, including residential zones. Due to the flammability of materials inside the facility, the device was estimated to have resulted in a 1-mile blast radius if it had gone off, Dixon said.
OUTAGES SWEEP ACROSS EVERY INDUSTRY: HERE’S WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW

The plant makes ethanol, a highly flammable liquid used in fuel, beverages, and hand sanitizer, along with ingredients for adhesives, detergents, and corn-based oils for renewable diesel, according to the company’s website . BioUrja bought the plant from Archer Daniels Midland in late 2021.

The Washington Examiner has reached out to BioUrja, the FBI’s Springfield office, the Peoria Police Department, and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of Illinois for further comment.

articles.headline: Resident Evil Requiem’s Game Awards Nominee Is Ready for Resident Evil 10
keyFacts: Actor Angela Sant'Albano received a 2026 Game Awards nomination for her performance as Grace Ashcroft in Resident Evil Requiem.
Sant'Albano utilized intense physical preparation and motion capture techniques to portray the character's anxiety and trauma.
Sant'Albano expressed interest in reprising her role as Grace in future Resident Evil titles to continue the character's story.
body: Angela Sant'Albano had never performed in a video game before Resident Evil Requiem. She'd never done motion capture, either. But after spending months physically throwing herself into the horror of Grace Ashcroft's story, she came away convinced that the medium was a perfect fit.
“I honestly couldn't have been luckier to be in Resident Evil,” Sant'Albano told Polygon a few weeks before her 2026 Game Awards nomination. “I still pinch myself.”
What surprised her most was how little she felt she had to change as a performer. Motion capture, she says, gave her the intimacy of television with the physical freedom of theater.

“Imagine you're doing theater in the round. So you have the audience 360 degrees around you, but then you have the intimacy of television and screen because you have a camera right here with you,” she says. “You can have an incredibly internal dialogue while also having the freedom of the body.”

And Requiem demanded plenty of body. The game's cutscenes were captured with the actors performing everything themselves, often in a darkened studio at London's Imaginarium Studios. Sant'Albano would run, fight, crawl, struggle, and generally work herself into a state of believable panic before scenes that required Grace to be gasping for breath.

“I would just run around, run around, do push ups, do jumping jacks, do whatever I could to keep my heart rate up,” she says. “Grace is a very anxious person. And yeah, sort of doing that when you kind of mimic anxiety in your body and mimic that breath, you then inevitably feel a bit anxious.”

Sometimes the production made the physical reality even more literal. In one early scene, Grace wakes up chained to a gurney. Sant'Albano was actually tilted around while lying upside down; when Grace gets dragged across the floor, Sant'Albano was dragged, too.
“I really believe that that is why the performances came across as so truthful,” she says, “because we put ourselves in a lot of those situations.”

That physical freedom extended to smaller choices, too. During rehearsals, Sant'Albano and the team were encouraged to push Grace's awkwardness and anxiety as far as they could, then pull it back. At one point, Sant'Albano decided there was one thing a terrified woman in her mid-20s would probably do more often.
“I just remember thinking like Grace is like a 25, 27-year-old girl. She's gonna swear,” she says. “How would Angela react in a lot of these situations? And I was like, she would say 'fuck.'”
So Capcom added swearing.

Finding Grace's voice itself came from digging into everything that made the character uncomfortable in her own skin. Sant'Albano researched stuttering extensively — when it happens, what can make it worse — before building the character from her traumatic history, her relationship with her mother, and her sense that she didn't quite belong at the FBI.
“I sort of just dived into her backstory in order to find her,” she says. “And then through that, like her voice and her posture ... it all kind of came weirdly naturally.”

Now Sant'Albano hopes that work wasn't a one-off. Grace survives Requiem, and her actor sees plenty of unfinished business: her mother's mysterious work, her relationship with Emily, and her growing bond with Leon Kennedy.
“I do hope that Grace will come back,” she says. “I think her story is definitely not over.” But if Grace does return, don't expect her to go full Sarah Connor in Terminator 2.
“She's never gonna be Leon,” she says. “And I think that's what makes her special.”

articles.headline: Michael van Gerwen forces broadcaster into issuing apology after swearing live on air
keyFacts: Michael van Gerwen beat Jeffrey de Graaf 5-4 on Tuesday to reach the knockout stage of the Grand Slam of Darts.
Sky Sports issued an apology after Van Gerwen used profanity during his live post-match interview.
Van Gerwen will next face seventh seed James Wade for a place in the quarter-finals.
body: Michael van Gerwen was involved in an X-rated post-match interview after surviving a scare at the Grand Slam of Darts.
The three-time champion beat Jeffrey de Graaf 5-4 on Tuesday night to progress to the knockout stage.
Sky Sports had to apologise during Van Gerwen’s post-match interview Getty
Van Gerwen had only needed to avoid losing by two legs or more to guarantee his place in the last 16.
Meanwhile, a 5-3 defeat would have seen group L decided on legs won against the throw for the first time in tournament history.
Fortunately for the Dutchman, he survived a comeback from De Graaf to edge out his opponent in a last leg decider.
Van Gerwen will now face seventh seed James Wade for a place in the quarter-finals.
Van Gerwen’s X-rated interview
Following the match, though, Sky Sports had to apologise for Mighty Mike’s language during his on-stage interview.
The 37-year-old admitted: “It wasn’t a good game at all. We were both put under a huge amount of pressure and it didn’t do us any favours, but it is what it is.
“I won luckily and I’m glad to be in the next round. I f***** up there, sorry. You know what I mean?
“Sometimes you’re not doing what you want to do and it’s frustrating because I know I’m capable of doing a lot more but what can I saw.
“I am through to the next round and onto the next one.”
His X-rated comment prompted reporter Abigail Davies to issue an immediate apology to viewers.
View Tweet: https://t.co/HSlnjsN233
She said: “We have to apologise there, of course. Tensions and emotions are running high.”
Van Gerwen has now made it past the first round of a PDC premier singles event for the first time since the World Matchplay in July.
It follows early exits at the World Grand Prix, European Championship and World Series of Darts Finals.
He is also back into the top ten in the world rankings after guaranteeing himself at least £20,000 in prize money.
Van Gerwen now sits ninth in the provisional rankings, but is still set to slip to 20th following the PDC World Darts Championship next month.
Who does Van Gerwen play next?
This week’s tournament sees the three-time world champion aiming to win the Grand Slam of Darts for the first time since 2017.
Van Gerwen will face Wade for a place in the Grand Slam quarter-finals Getty
That triumph was the third of three in a row for Van Gerwen at the event.
Wade is now standing between him and the 11th quarter-final appearance of his career.
Looking ahead to their match, Van Gerwen added: “James Wade is playing some fantastic darts.
“I need to bring my A-game if I am going to beat him- simple as that.”
The winner of their clash will face either Luke Humphries or Tom Sykes in the last eight.

articles.headline: WoW Forever Undead Paladin guide (Best spec, quests and what to press)
keyFacts: World of Warcraft: Forever allows players to create Undead Paladins, which is the only Horde race currently able to access the Paladin class.
Undead Paladins can utilize unique racial abilities like Will of the Forsaken and Cannibalize while managing mana as their primary resource for combat.
Players can choose between Retribution for solo questing, Protection for tanking, or Holy for healing, with specific stat priorities recommended for each specialization.
body: The Undead Paladin is one of the biggest surprises of World of Warcraft: Forever , since the game’s redo on the OG launch experience actually gives the Horde a shot to get a crack on the Paladin Class later on.

You can sink your teeth in The Forsaken Kingdom to get the specifics on the lore, but the TL;DR is that the Light didn’t have a reason to abandon the Undead, who technically didn’t choose to be Undead in the first place.
So now you created your Undead, and you’re roaming around Tirisfal Glades with the ability to tank for others and do heals on the side. What else should you consider?
Table of contents
Enter the Undead
The starter Paladin spells to take note of
The go-to starter Undead Paladin rotation while you prepare your spec
The Paladin specs at a glance in WoW: Forever
The stats your Undead Paladin wants
The best Professions for an Undead Paladin
Retribution Paladin: A quick look at the talent tree Use this rotation for the Retribution Paladin
Build: Retribution usually stays pure
Protection Paladin: A quick look at the talent tree Use this rotation for the Protection Paladin
Build: Protection should take a few points in Retribution
Holy Paladin: A quick look at the talent tree Use this rotation for the Holy Paladin
Build: Holy can take a few points in Retribution
Enter the Undead

Creating an Undead Paladin in World of Warcraft: Forever. Screenshot by Destructoid The Undead serves as the only Horde Race to access to the Paladin Class (as of launch) since we don’t have Blood Elves at this point in Forever ’s story. In the lore, the sacrifice of Garek Bandarion in The Forsaken Kingdom reminded his Forsaken brethren that there is still a chance for their kind to access the Light, even if their bodies hurt from doing it.
In the game, this means your Paladin can benefit from the full slate of the Undead’s Racial Abilities:

Ability Nature What is it Will of the Forsaken Active Removes Charm, Fear, and Sleep (2-min cooldown) Cannibalize Active Heal 7 percent of Health and Mana every two seconds for 10s from a Humanoid or Undead corpse Touch of the Grave Passive Five percent chance that Spells and Attacks lifesteal up to five percent of your max Health Underwater Breathing Passive Breathe underwater for 4x longer The starter Paladin spells to take note of

A lot of the Paladin talents you’ll encounter from Level 10 onwards are more to build what you’ll eventually focus on, but the way you kill your enemies can be “standardized” by combining these above with some early-level spells from the playstyle of the spec you prefer (more on them below).

Level Spell What it does 1 Holy Light Turn spare mana into health in between fights 1 Devotion Aura Lowers the damage you take, before Retribution Aura 4 Judgment Release your current Seal to deal damage, doesn’t affect your swing 6 Holy Strike Instant Holy melee, doesn’t affect your swing 6 Divine Protection Immunity to all damage for a brief moment 8 Hammer of Justice Your only stun (single-target) 10 Lay on Hands All of your mana for a full heal 10 Blessing of Protection Immunity to Physical Damage 12 Redemption If you finish “A Lesson in Divinity” then you get this resurrection spell 16 Retribution Aura Enemies get damaged when they hit you, which is perfect for leveling post-Devotion Aura 18 Blessing of Freedom Removes stuns and slows 20 Consecration Nearby AoE 20 Exorcism Big instant Holy damage on Undead and Demons 20 Blessing of Kings Raises all stats The go-to starter Undead Paladin rotation while you prepare your spec
The focus of these rotations is always on mana, since this is your damage and healing resource. There will only be alternate rotations if you want to start focusing on a spec later on.

Level Use this rotation What changes, if any 1-3 Seal of Righteousness -> Auto Attack Always have Devotion Aura to reduce damage, then use Holy Light if you are low 4-5 S. Righteousness -> Judgment If your next Auto Attack kills, then don’t use Judgment 6-9 S. Righteousness -> Judgment -> Holy Strike Divine Protection if you need the emergency immunity 10-15 S. Righteousness -> Judgment -> Holy Strike -> Blessing of Protection as a reset on bad pulls Lay on Hands if you are dangerously low 16-19 S. Righteousness -> Judgment -> Holy Strike -> Hammer of Justice if you want to stop runners or buy time for heal Switch Devotion Aura to Retribution Aura for damage reflect 20 Blessing of Kings -> Consecration on mobs -> S. Righteousness -> Judgment -> Holy Strike Add Exorcism when fighting Undead or Demons, then don’t use Consecration if the pack will likely die before if finishes the full damage Holy Light is your core healing, which can evolve into Divine Protection or Lay on Hands depending on the situation. Judgment and Holy Strike are cheap and don’t affect your swings, so they’re your primary damage dealers, but skip them if your next strike will kill your target.
The Paladin specs at a glance in WoW: Forever

Undead Paladin casting a spell in WoW Forever. Image via Blizzard Entertainment Unlike the other versions of WoW , the class progression i n Forever uses the OG iteration of the Talent System , essentially allowing you to take points across any of your preferred talent trees to make your ideal “build.” And while you have the freedom to be as creative as possible, your Undead Paladin can maximize their toolkit if they lean into how these specs are usually played:

Retribution: This is the most practical spec for solo questing, and it can feel very “fast” killing single targets with your abilities. Your Consecration can hit up to four targets at once, but you’ll still be feeling very focused on one-at-a-time mob clearing.

Protection: This is the tanking spec, which makes it the go-to tree for groups. Your taunts can feel very powerful and very effective in getting the heat off your teammates. You won’t kill your targets as fast, but it does make you very hard to hit.

Holy: This is the healing spec. You’ll feel a slowdown in your solo leveling, but you can provide heals where necessary, especially when your healer is down or is busy healing others. Holy can make you very independent, but it lacks firepower.
The stats your Undead Paladin wants

Your Undead Paladin will get their damage from mainly your weapon swings and Holy damage overall. In your rotations, that’s going to be your autoattacks (scales with the weapon and Strength) and your Judgments, Holy Strikes, Consecrations and Seals (grows with Spell Power) that cost mana (which comes from Intellect). Since you already know what the specs are, here’s their general stats priority:

Spec Priority Why these Retribution Strength and Attack Power, Weapon DPS, Hit, Agility, Intellect, Spell Power, Critical Strike The weapon you use decides what Seal you use (2H for Command, fast for Righteousness), then Hit for your Seals, Judgment, and Holy Protection Stamina, Spell Power, Strength, Block, Hit, Defense, Armor, Intellect, Agility Stamina is priority since you need that survive the pull itself, then Spell Power so Consecration and Holy Shield are stronger, with Block a good investment for all your defensive talents Holy Spirit, Intellect, Healing Power, Critical Strike, Haste Spirit and Intellect facilitate Mana regen, then Critical Strike for improved heals and a talent that refunds mana on crit, Haste to ensure you secure your heals fast enough The best Professions for an Undead Paladin

With the new adjustments on Spell Power and equipment , your Undead Paladin will can get more out of their spells and heals with the right kind of gear. And similar to other melee and hybrid Classes, your Paladin will have a plethora of potential equipment to wear as you start dungeoneering or do more raiding. But if you want to double down on a Profession so you can create your own gear, here are the ideal ones for you to choose:

Mining and Blacksmithing: This is a natural one-two-punch combo since Blacksmithing is the only profession that makes mail and plate with Spell Power and healing for your class. There’s a set that is perfect for your damage (Crusader’s and Justicar’s for Retribution), tank (Guard’s, Warder’s, and Sentinel’s for Protection), and healer (Acolyte’s and Prefect’s for Holy) specs.

Engineering: This is a decent alternative once you fill up on Mining since you can get gadgets that compensate for your lack of frequent pulls, slows, and interrupts. Gadgets and trinkets here ensure you don’t waste mana but still achieve similar control effects that other classes enjoy.
Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter !
Retribution Paladin: A quick look at the talent tree

Retribution Paladin in WoW Forever. Image via Blizzard Entertainment The Retribution Paladin fights alone. Your damage won’t come from big spells but instead through your Seal, which gives a bit of Holy damage per swing. You can alternate your Seal of Righteousness with Seal of the Crusader if you prefer faster and hard-hitting attacks with less overall damage, but your Judgments do more Holy damage.

Level Spell What it does 4 Blessing of Might Get more Attack Power before Blessing of Kings 6 Seal of the Crusader Faster and more Attack Power for less damage in general, but Judgments do more Holy damage Level Spell What it does 22 Seal of Command Deal 70 percent of normal weapon damage as extra Holy damage, Judgments deal more damage on stunned enemies 33 Repentance Stun up to six seconds, but wakes them on damage 34 Divine Shield Immune to damage and damage of your attacks get reduced by 50 percent Row Talent What it does 3 Pursuit of Justice (2/2) Get more run and mount speed 3 Seal of Command (1/1) Teaches Seal of Command 4 Two-Handed Weapon Specialization (3/3) Get more Physical and Holy damage when using a two-hander 5 Vengeance (3/3) Adds three percent damage per crit, stackable up to five times 5 Repentance (1/1) Unlocks Repentance 6 Champion of the Light (5/5) Spell damage upped based on Intellect, reduces Hammer of Wrath casting time 7 Unsealed Wrath (1/1) Melee attacks can store a copy of the Seal up to three times, then landing with a different Seal will consume all stored stacks From Level 20, Seal of Command gives you more Holy damage and Judgments now deal more damage to stunned enemies, which is perfect by the time you get your stronger stuns with Repentance . For emergencies, go for immunity with Divine Shield in exchange for reduced attack damage.
Use this rotation for the Retribution Paladin
Level Use this What changes 10-21 Blessing of Might -> Seal of Righteousness -> Judgment -> Holy Strike Switch Might to King when you reach Level 20

If you’re in a long fight, use Seal of the Crusader and Judge it first then switch to Judging with Seal of Righteousness afterwards 22-32 Seal of Command -> Hammer of Justice -> Judgment -> Holy Strike -> Consecration on packs Use Seal of Righteousness if you have a fast weapon or if you’ve stocked up on Spell Power
Stick with Seal of Righteousness if you prefer heavier-hitting Holy damage Judges

Then use Exorcism if you’re fighting Undead and Demons 33 Seal of Command -> Repentance -> Judgment -> Holy Strike -> Consecration on packs Use Repentance with Judgment if you’re fighting humans, then switch to Hammer of Justice on beasts and undead 34-39 Seal of Command -> Repentance -> Judgment -> Holy Strike -> Consecration on packs -> Divine Shield when a pull goes back If you put points in Champion of the Light and have decent Intellect and Spell Power, you can switch Seal of Command to Righteousness 40 Swap Seals after stacking copies to trigger Unsealed Wrath – Every fight runs the same way. You Seal up, then Judgment and Holy Strike on cooldowns, with autoattacks handling the rest. Things switch up when you get access to your second Seal, since you adjust based on your preference. You’d go for Seal of the Crusader and Judgment that to make later Holy hits (Holy Strike, other Seals, Consecration, optional Exorcism) land harder without affecting your swing.

Switch to Seal of Command if you can manage having a slower two-hander with a stronger kick, or Seal of Righteousness if you want to take advantage of Spell Power. Hammer of Justice evolves into Repentance for your stun and you use that with Judgment so they drop at the same time.
Build: Retribution usually stays pure

Retribution prioritizes damage and speed, none of which the other two trees prioritize. Protection is best used with a shield, whereas Holy’s talents cater to heals, both of which the Retribution Paladin doesn’t really care much for. There’s not a lot of incentive to diversify a Retribution build, since you’ll default to this if you prefer the midpoint between tank and DPS as a Paladin.

Ideally, you’d invest your points to get Champion of the Light so you get more stuns out of your Hammer of Justice, and eventually Unsealed Wrath to stack your Seals for devastating damage. The only setbacks are that there’s no active answer to spellcasters, there’s no immediate way of slowing runners, and it’s generally weak on range. But when you get on melee, your damage output can be devastating.
Protection Paladin: A quick look at the talent tree

Protection Paladin fighting a monster in WoW Forever. Image via Blizzard Entertainment If you want your Undead Paladin to tank, then definitely go for Protection . You don’t care much for damage, but instead want to build enough toughness to outlast enemies you’re taunting to keep on hitting you instead of everyone else. This is why your Seal of Fury now makes your Judgments also come with a taunt while some of your other abilities also give back mana. Getting threat via Righteous Fury becomes second nature, and Consecration becomes a best friend to ensure you always hit mobs.

Level Spell What it does Trainer Righteous Fury Adds threat (better in dungeons) 10 Seal of Fury Using a shield can absorb some damage, and Judgments now have Taunt Level Spell What it does 20 Templar’s Bulwark Absorb shield equal to your max Health for a few seconds 25 Swift Judgment Second Judgment that taunts 30 Holy Shield Increases block chance and each block sends back an attack (up to four blocks), and Holy Strike generates more threat 30 Divine Intervention Save the healer on a wipe so they can resurrect 34 Divine Shield Protects from all damage in exchange for half-damage done Row Talent What it does 1 Redoubt (5/5) When a melee attack damages you, it also has a 10% chance to give you six percent chance to block. Lasts 10s or five blocks 3 Templar’s Bulwark (1/1) Unlocks Templar’s Bulwark 3 Shield Specialization (2/2) Shields can block more damage and has 50 percent chance to return some mana on a block 4 Swift Judgment (1/1 Teaches Swift Judgment 4 Improved Righteous Fury (3/3) Righteous Fury now reduces damage taken 5 Holy Shield (1/1) Unlocks Holy Shield 5 Reckoning (5/5) If you block or receive crits, you can gain up to four extra attacks 7 Shieldsworn (1/1) Holy Strike has a smaller cooldown and strikes with your shield. It triggers your Holy Shield and Shield Specialization talents with no charges/CDs Talents-wise, your Protection Paladin will also be better-equipped to take more blows than the other Paladin types can carry. Shield Specialization ensures you get mana back on hit, then Holy Shield unlocks a way to block hits while hitting back at the same time. With Reckoning , those hits on you become extra attacks as well. Most importantly, mastering Templar’s Bulwark for the additional protection means you have a lot of ways to survive even the worst of pulls.
Use this rotation for the Protection Paladin

Level Use this rotation What changes 10-19 Seal of Righteousness -> Righteous Fury in groups -> Judgment to taunt -> Holy Strike If you’re questing solo then switch to Seal of Righteousness, then Seal of Fury in dungeons 20-24 S. of Righteousness -> Righteous Fury in groups -> Consecration -> Judgment -> Holy Strike -> Templar’s Bulwark when health drops Careful when using Temple’s Bulwark since using it gets you Forbearance (1min) which locks you out of Divine Protection and Divine Shield 25-29 Same as above, but when Judgment is on cooldown then do

S. of Fury -> Righteous Fury in groups -> Consecration -> Swift Judgment -> Holy Strike -> Templar’s Bulwark when health drops You need Seal of Fury to taunt with Swift Judgment 30-39 Holy Shield -> S. of Righteousness -> Righteous Fury in groups -> Consecration -> Judgment -> Holy Strike -> Templar’s Bulwark when health drops Use Devotion Aura instead of Retribution Aura if another Paladin is running Retribution 40 S. of Righteousness -> Righteous Fury in groups -> Consecration -> Judgment -> Holy Strike -> Templar’s Bulwark when health drops Use Holy Strike whenever available as Shieldsworn lowers its CD The idea of a rotation with a Protection Tank is to get threat on everything first, then use your survival tools when something turns sideways. Mana and blocks are your lifeline here, so talents like Redoubt, Shield Specialization and Holy Shield turn blocks into mana, damage, and even additional defense.

Rotations open with Sealing up with Fury then go Judgment to ensure the mobs aggro on you, which you then punish with Consecration. When you unlock Holy Shield, that comes out first since any hits you get will give back Mana for your next Consecrations. Holy Strike fills the gaps, then Swift Judgment is insurance that any mob will run back to you even if an ally out-aggros you.
Build: Protection should take a few points in Retribution

Row Talent What it does Replaces Retribution 1 Benediction (5) -10 percent Mana cost on instants, and Consecration is easier to keep up Reckoning (5, row five) Retribution 2 Conviction (3) +Six percent critical strike chance Iron Creed (3, row six) Retribution 2 Improved Judgment (2) Get Judgment and its taunt for 2s sooner Anticipation (2, row four) Borrowing from Retribution makes sense for most of your Paladin’s leveling process, given you’ll spend most of your time in-game questing instead of in dungeons, at least for now. The only setback here is that Templar’s Bulwark gets to you at the most at Level 34, Swift Judgment at 37, and Holy Shield after you dual spec. But in exchange, you get less Mana on instants ( Benediction ) and secure your Judgments much faster ( Improved Judgment ).

If you pursue this build, treat your Protection Paladin as a Retribution Paladin until around level 21 before you start investing points into the Protection tree. By the time you go 40, that’s when you dual spec into Retribution or respec into a full defensive build.
Holy Paladin: A quick look at the talent tree

Holy Paladin in WoW Forever. Image via Blizzard Entertainment Pursue a Holy build if you want your Undead Paladin to keep everyone alive. This tree will build the Paladin like an actual healer, so the expectation here is that you’ll “read” who’s taking damage and pick the right heal based on the circumstances. Thankfully, you do have decent heals for most occasions, whether one-shot emergencies ( Flash of Light ), standard single-targets ( Holy Light ), or AoEs ( Light’s Vigil into Holy Shock ). Just remember, your heals won’t be as potent as a Priest’s , so set your expectations carefully.

Level Spell What it does Trainer Flash of Light Your most efficient heal, and usually your group heal 8 Purify Remove a disease and poison from a party member 14 Blessing of Wisdom Restore mana over time Level Spell What it does 25 Oath of Light Five-minute healing boost to a chosen ally 30 Seal of Light Attacks and Judgments have a chance to heal the Paladin 30 Holy Shock Instantly heal an ally or damage an enemy 30 Divine Intervention Saves a healer from a wipe so they can prepare for a rez 31 Divine Favor Next heal is a guaranteed critical 40 Light’s Vigil Next Holy Shock heals the entire party Row
Talent

What it does 1 Spiritual Focus (5/5) Get a chance to not lose casting time when you take damage while casting Flash of Light, Holy Light, and Light’s Vigil 3 Illumination (5) On a crit, 20 percent chance to gain 50 percent of the mana cost of casting Flash of Light, Holy Light, Light’s Vigil, or Holy Shock 4 Oath of Light (1/1) Teaches Oath of Light 5 Holy Shock (1/1) Unlocks Holy Shock 3 Divine Favor (1/1) Unlocks Divine Favor 6 Holy Power (5/5) Increase the critical strike healing of Holy spells up to 50 percent 7 Light’s Vigil (1/1) Teach Light’s Vigil Likewise, Holy Paladins have some talents to take them to the next level. With Spiritual Focus , you can keep healing without being pushed back even on hits. Then with Illumination , your crits can heal more thanks to refunds. Plus Holy Power can make crits heal more. Sadly, the best Holy Paladin talents aren’t damage-oriented, so you’re slow when leveling alone.
Use this rotation for the Holy Paladin

Level Rotation What changes 10-24 Seal of Righteousness -> Judgment -> Holy Strike -> Holy Light after fights on solo and Flash of Light in groups Use Holy Light over Flash of Light only when there is heavy damage and you can afford it 25-29 Oath of Light before the pull -> S. of Righteousness -> Judgment -> Holy Strike -> Holy Light or Flash of Light Only one Oath at a time 30 Same as above but
Seal of Light whenever you focus on healing, Holy Shock for emergencies or while moving Only use Holy Shock in emergencies as it uses a lot of mana 31-39 Same as above but

Divine Favor before a Holy Light in emergencies Boundless Light only boosts Holy Shock on allies without your Oath, so Shock non-tanks 40 Use Light’s Vigil on a target before heavy group damage, then Holy Shock that target to heal the party Illumination refuns mana only once when Light’s Vigil heal crits several targets The best Holy Paladin rotations revolve around group plays, so they’re not as effective if you’re trying to heal yourself as compared to when you have a partner or some companions to fill other spots. In groups, you buff the tank with Oath of Light so they take more heals, then keep them alive with Flash of Light and use Holy Light on them when there are heavy hits. At 40, Light’s Vigil facilitates your only group heal, but otherwise it’s really alternating between the two Lights to keep everyone alive.

Compared to other healers, the Paladin isn’t ideally someone to go “pure” heal given they can be effective tanks as well. They work well as a sub-healer, or an emergency healer if the Priest, Shaman, or Druid is down. By the time you reach Level 25, expect to feel somewhat like a “slower” Retribution Paladin, since the talents that normally help the Retribution build get faster and hit harder are instead reserved for your heals.
Build: Holy can take a few points in Retribution

Row Talent What it does Replaces Retribution 1 Benediction (5/5) Reduce Mana cost on instants by 10 percent Holy Power (4, row six) and Light’s Vigil (1, row seven) Retribution 2 Conviction (3/3) Adds six percent critical hit chance for all spells and attacks Boundless Light (2, row five) and Divine Favor (1, row three) Retribution 2 Improved Judgment (2/2) Judgment arrives 2s sooner Consecrated Ground (2, row five) Similar to Discipline, the best dip for a Holy Paladin is by giving yourself a few points in Retribution. The argument is similar in nature; this time instead of trading off defense (Protection) for offensive power, you’re forcing your strongest heals to come much later in exchange for some leveling convenience early on.

With Conviction , you’re giving yourself more room for mana refunds with Illumination since you’re getting more crit chance. Again, this does push Oath of Life as far as potentially Level 37, so you might have to do additional healing to your party. At 40, your healer will be much faster until you finally get Holy Shock with the dual spec.

articles.headline: GOP Senator Ashley Moody missed vote after DC-bound flight grounded due to engine problems
keyFacts: Republican Senator Ashley Moody missed Senate votes after her Washington, DC-bound flight experienced engine failure.
Officials said the American Airlines flight from Tampa was forced to make an emergency landing in Orlando on Monday.
Moody spokesperson William O’Grady confirmed the incident, which occurred shortly after the plane departed.
body: A Republican congresswoman missed Senate votes after her flight from Florida to Washington, DC was forced to make an emergency landing due to engine problems on Monday, officials said.

American Airlines Flight 496 carrying Sen. Ashley Moody (R-Fla.) made a detour to Orlando shortly after taking off from Tampa International Airport, Moody spokesperson William O’Grady told First Coast News.
“Yesterday, the American Airlines flight Senator Moody was on had engine failure and had to make an emergency landing in Orlando,” her spokesperson said.

articles.headline: Slow down a bit and help a cow find a friend in the lush-looking, hand-drawn, milk deliver-em-up Milki Delivery, which is out now
keyFacts: The video game Milki Delivery was released today on Steam.
Players control a character named Neha who delivers milk to help her pet cow find a friend.
The game features a mouse-driven navigation system and allows players to create different milk types by feeding the cow various ingredients.
body: I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

The stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

It's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.
In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

articles.headline: Meta Tests Direct, a Standalone Chat App Just for Your Instagram DMs
keyFacts: Meta is testing a standalone texting app named Direct for Instagram DMs in Turkey and Thailand.
The iOS and Android app allows messaging with or without an Instagram account and includes personalization features.
Meta stated that the app requires age verification and blocks users under 13.
body: Meta is testing a new texting app, giving your Instagram DMs a dedicated place away from the app’s feed and stories. The Direct app, announced on Monday, is currently being tested in Turkey and Thailand. There’s no date yet on when it might expand to other countries.

Available on both iOS and Android, the Direct app largely mirrors Instagram’s texting feature. It sounds similar to Meta’s Messenger app, which itself spun out of Facebook for texts and video calls. And it would also join WhatsApp, so the company certainly has no shortage of different ways to text.

The Direct app includes several features for personalizing your conversations, including drawing, custom stickers, voice effects and chat background themes. You can also use it with or without an Instagram account, which could be particularly useful for someone who wants to text someone on the platform but intentionally doesn’t want a profile on the service. When using the service without a full Instagram account, you can add others by username or by scanning a QR code.
More from CNET

Across Meta’s chat apps, the company has taken different approaches to end-to-end encryption and privacy. Instagram’s conversations aren’t currently encrypted, whereas those on Messenger and WhatsApp are.

Meta says the Direct app will require users to verify their age and will use technology to block anyone under 13 from using the chat app. The service will also provide similar protections for teen accounts as are currently offered in the main Instagram app.

articles.headline: Former world boxing champion Jorge Linares detained by ICE in Texas
keyFacts: Former world boxing champion Jorge Linares was detained by ICE at the Texas border, according to federal records and his social media posts.
Linares's legal representation stated that the retired Venezuelan fighter is legally present in the United States and is cooperating fully with authorities.
Lawyers said they expect the matter to be resolved after the immigration process concludes, while the WBA president confirmed he is in contact with the family.
body: Former world boxing champion Jorge Linares has been detained by US immigration authorities in Texas, despite his lawyers insisting the retired Venezuelan fighter is legally in the country.

Linares is being held at the El Paso Processing Center, according to federal detention records reviewed by the San Antonio Express-News. The circumstances of his detention remain unclear, while US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has not publicly explained why he was taken into custody.
The 41-year-old boxing great, who captured titles across three weight classes from featherweight to lightweight, first disclosed his detention in a post on X on Sunday.
“ICE has me at the Texas border crossing. This is crazy,” Linares wrote in Spanish. He has not posted publicly since.
The immigration law firm Wilner & O’Reilly, which is representing Linares, confirmed his detention on Monday and said he was legally present in the United States.

“Mr Linares is legally present in the United States and has cooperated fully with the authorities,” the firm said in a statement. “We are working closely with ICE and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to resolve this matter as quickly as possible.”

Linares’s lawyers said they were confident in their client’s legal position and expected the matter to be resolved once the immigration process had concluded. They also asked supporters and the media for patience.
Gilberto Mendoza, president of the World Boxing Association (WBA), confirmed Linares’ detention and said he was in regular contact with the fighter’s family.

“His case is in the hands of immigration lawyers, and I am in constant contact with his family,” Mendoza wrote on X. “As WBA president, I will always support our champions, inside and outside the ring. Stay strong, Jorge.”
Linares, who fought out of Las Vegas under the nickname El Niño de Oro (the Golden Boy), was regarded as one of boxing’s most gifted technicians during his 21-year professional career.

He won his first world championship at 126lb in 2007 before adding titles at 130lb and 135lb. His most successful period came at lightweight, where he held versions of the WBA and WBC world titles between 2014 and 2018.

His reign at 135lb ended in a memorable showdown with Vasiliy Lomachenko at Madison Square Garden in May 2018. Linares knocked down the heavily favored Ukrainian with a right hand in the sixth round and pushed him to the limit before being stopped by a body shot in the 10th.
Linares retired in October 2023 after losing to Britain’s Jack Catterall in Liverpool, ending his career with a record of 47 wins, including 29 knockouts, and nine defeats.
The Guardian contacted ICE’s El Paso field office and national media office for comment but had received no response by Tuesday evening.

articles.headline: Does Jesus Christ Exist In World Of Warcraft?
keyFacts: World of Warcraft players hear a song featuring Latin lyrics singing Agnus Dei, which means Lamb of God, when their character dies.
The author questions why this religious music is used in the game and whether it implies the existence of a Christian afterlife in Azeroth.
The author is requesting an explanation from Blizzard and the game's composers regarding the inclusion of these specific lyrics.
body: When you die in World of Warcraft, regardless of whether you’re playing Classic or retail or Forever or whatever (as long as you’re not playing hardcore mode), the same thing happens every time.

First, you get a little pop-up window that invites you to get a “recap” of how you died and will tell you what moves did damage to you and how much. That same window also has a “Release Spirit” option which you’ll have to press eventually if you want to keep playing.

When you hit “Release Spirit,” you’re transported to the nearest Graveyard, which may or may not be located a whole-ass ten-minute walk from where you died. Your screen will appear in black and white with a ghostly filter. Your character will not be able to interact with anything, use items, speak, or really do much of anything except move. And move you must, back to your corpse, at which point you can return to your body and continue with whatever you were doing before. Alternatively, you can resurrect yourself at the graveyard, but doing so will break your equipment and give you a horrible ten-minute debuff, so it’s not recommended except in dire situations.

But let’s go back to those moments when you’re running back to your dead body and everything is all ghostly. There’s some music playing while you’re doing that. It’s the same, again, in every version of WoW, and always has been. This is it:
All right, now what in the gosh darn heck is going on here?

Listen to that music. Hear those vocals? Know what they’re singing? It’s not some made-up video game language, people! That there isÂ Latin, the traditional language of the Roman Catholic Church, and those voices are singing “Agnus Dei” over and over, loud and clear. Agnus Dei, for those who did not grow up participating in the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass, means “Lamb of God.” It’s referring toÂ Jesus Christ, specifically as he’s referred to by John the Baptist in the Bible book of John (not the Baptist).

Has anyone else ever thought this was super goofy? Just me? Very, very few songs in World of Warcraft have lyrics. Most of the background music is purely instrumental, intended to be thematic and ambient to your journey. There are a few pieces with vocals, but almost every time they come up, they’re either a sort of non-descript chorus of Ahhhs and Ohhhs, or they’re sung in an actual language invented for this fictional video game. See one of my absolute faves, “Nightsong” from the Cataclysm expansion. It’s in elf language:

So I return to: Why is there a single song in World of Warcraft, a song that’s been in the game since its inception and which every single player has to listen to repeatedly if they have the music on in every incarnation of the game, in which a chorus of voices are singing the Agnus Dei? What could this possibly be meant to imply? Are the words “Agnus Dei” meaningful in some way to the people of Azeroth? Is there some sort of Christian afterlife attached to this world? I feel like that can’t be right given everything we went through in Shadowlands, but I think the takeaway from that expansion is that there are many different afterlives, including many we don’t see. Could that mean that a heaven with Jesus in it exists somewhere, and our WoW characters are destined for it when we die for real?

Did Jesus die for the sins of the people of Azeroth, too? Is he the Lamb of God who takes away the sins of all the worlds, including Azeroth? Because good Lord, there’s a lot of sinning going on down there. Lots of violence, murder, and such. Whatever the Warlock Succubus pet is doing certainly isn’t permitted by the Ten Commandments. Azerothians almost assuredly need whatever salvation they can get.

I do not want to simply believe that the answer is “Someone thought it sounded cool once.” I refuse, and am instead demanding accountability from Blizzard, Jason Hayes, Glenn Stafford, Derek Duke, and Tracy W. Bush. I would also be willing to hear from any theologians who have opinions on this. My email inbox is open and waiting to hear your explanation. In the meantime, I am dead again thanks to the assholes over in Dun Garok who don’t want to share Humbert’s Sword with me, so I will be listening to “Agnus Dei” on loop for the next several minutes and reminding myself of the life, death, and resurrection of Christ.

articles.headline: Wales beaten by 10-man Portugal as Neto scores but is sent off
keyFacts: Wales lost 3-2 to Portugal in their final UEFA Nations League group match at Cardiff City Stadium.
Portugal finished at the top of the group despite Pedro Neto being sent off for two yellow cards in the second half.
Wales finished bottom of the group and will compete in a relegation/promotion play-off in March.
body: Wales vs Portugal; UEFA Nations League Group A4
Wales vs Portugal. UEFA Nations League Group A4.
Cardiff City Stadium.
Wales 2-3 Portugal: Craig Bellamy's side lose final Nations League Group A4 match as Pedro Neto sent off

Match report as Wales lose final Nations League Group A4 game to 10-man Portugal in a 3-2 home defeat; Man Utd's Bruno Fernandes hit opener; Chelsea's Pedro Neto scored Portugal's second but was sent off in second half for two bookings in two minutes; Portugal finish top with Wales bottom
Tuesday 17 November 2026 22:32, UK
Wales ended their Nations League group campaign with a 3-2 defeat against 10-man Portugal in Cardiff after Chelsea's Pedro Neto was sent off.

Although there was little riding on the contest, with Wales guaranteed a League A relegation/promotion play-off in March and Portugal having qualified for the quarter-finals, the two sides produced an entertaining spectacle.
Portugal skipper Bruno Fernandes blasted the opener after 11 minutes, but that was immediately wiped out by David Brooks' ninth goal for Wales.
Sorba Thomas broke free to put Wales ahead before the break, but again there was a quickfire response as Neto pounced to restore parity.

Substitute Carlos Forbs stroked Portugal ahead in the final quarter, and the visitors had to negotiate the final 16 minutes a player short after Neto was sent off after receiving two yellow cards in the space of two minutes.
Wales finish bottom of League A4 with one win and five defeats, and end a disappointing 2026 with a solitary victory, three draws and six losses from 10 games.
Portugal, meanwhile, finish the campaign as group winners as they earned their first win since Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement.
How Wales lost five-goal thriller...
Craig Bellamy's side had lost 1-0 in Lisbon in September in a game that was to prove Ronaldo's last for Portugal.

Ronaldo's subsequent retirement from international football probably had an impact on the attendance at Cardiff City Stadium, with some seats unfilled, despite the game being officially declared a sell-out.
There would be no clean sheet for Danny Ward on his 50th appearance as Joao Neves robbed Josh Sheehan and Fernandes lashed home from the edge of the box.

Wales responded immediately with Rubin Colwill twice involved, first setting up Harry Wilson for a shot Diogo Costa blocked with his legs and then Brooks, who swept home his ninth international goal, and second in two games.
Wales hit the front five minutes before the break after Brooks worked a one-two with Wilson before releasing Thomas, who advanced from his own half to slot past Costa.
The lead lasted three minutes as Neto lost Jay DaSilva from Trincao's cross to finish at the far post.

A breathless first half was not finished as Wilson hit the roof of the net from halfway with Costa retreating frantically, and the Leeds midfielder then forced a sprawling save from the Portugal goalkeeper.

Portugal regained the lead 20 minutes from time when Club Brugge winger Forbs - wearing Portugal's new-styled number seven shirt in the post-Ronaldo era - collected Ben Cabango's poor header and stepped inside Ben Davies to find the bottom corner.
Neto clattered into Brennan Johnson just one minute and 59 seconds after being booked, but Portugal held on for a fifth Nations League win to seal top spot.
Bellamy: That summed up the group for us
Wales head coach Craig Bellamy to BBC Sport:

"We knew in moments we were going to have to suffer due to the quality they have. The intensity wasn't there. We have a lot of players who don't play week in, week out a high-tempo game in such a short space of time. It's not ideal.

"We knew that at moments, when we win it, the spaces open. There were moments that worked really well. It summed up the group for us - really good moments for us; we make a mistake - at this level, these are normal things that happen.
"But also, that final moment. These teams have that profile to hurt you. At both ends, that last bit has caught us a bit in this group.

"Rubin Colwill is really good. There are times where he takes too many touches. You can't do that against this type of team. Five, six, seven - no! When he motors like he has, the ability to be a real top-end player. I'm very critical of him; I do love him.
"But I know there's more. That's why I wanted to play him in this A league. He's going to have to prove himself."
Wilson: We were better team in large spells
Wales forward Harry Wilson to BBC Sport:
"For large parts, we played really well again. At times in the first half, we had to suffer. They're a great team full of world-class stars. At times in our shape, we were comfy.
"But look at our three goals. We're disappointed. But for large parts we were really, really good again.
"We knew from the start it was going to be tough. The first game in the group against Portugal, we showed we belong. Against Norway, we beat them. In large spells tonight, we were the better team.
"Going forward or defending the goal a bit better, that's what we've got to focus on. We're going toe-to-toe with these teams; our shape is good off the ball."
